ActionSpent.word.why: turns.py:519 is the one door and emits ActionSpent(actor=eid, cost=what) -- cost is an ActionType, so standing up is indistinguishable from any other move-costed action. The caller knows the word; the event has no field for it.

Attack(vs=).why: c.attacks_defence moves a creature's attacks onto another defence, registers in Window.BEFORE, and takes a when= that "reads the attack context" and a from_= that narrows to attacks starting on a named defence. Its docstring is written against exactly this error: "The engine has always allowed this and the rows said it did not."

Attack(vs=several).found: c.attacks_defence from an interrupt -- resolve.roll reads vs = declared.vs
Attack(vs=several).why: p15953's own docstring settles it: 'Correction: the defence is not header-only and the verb exists ... This row is writable -- it needs its card read, not an engine change. #509.' The marker outlived the correction.

Budget.opportunity_turn.found: components.Budget.opportunity_turn, turns.py stamping it at 502/527, content precedent writing Budget by hand (powers/battlemind/level_7 sets budget.standard = 0)
Budget.opportunity_turn.why: The cap is one stamp compared against the current turn, and content rows already reach Budget directly, so a watcher that clears the stamp lifts it. The printed narrowing ('enemies it has marked') is askable in the same watcher, so the row is writable without a verb.

Cast.forbid(usage=).why: c.forbid already bans by keyword as well as by ref, through a parallel set on Powers -- a forbidden_usages set is the same shape. Not run down: m5559a4's line is 'encounter or daily *attack* powers', which needs the attack half too, so it may be two gates rather than one.

Cast.kill().why: The verb exists and m1978a5's own docstring already says so ('**Re-pointed.** `c.kill` exists now and is not what this waits on'). m5559a2 still carries `todo=("Cast.kill()",)` over a written body -- a stale marker.

Cast.summon(hp=).found: c.summon returns the new eid; content precedent for writing components by hand (monsters.level_12.controllers_sa._strips_resistance, monsters.level_11.brutes._take_resistances); monsters.level_12.controllers._acts_after_its_creator
Cast.summon(hp=).why: The clone's hit points can be set on the returned entity's Health the way other rows edit Defences directly, and moving the new creature's slot under its creator -- the shared initiative count -- is already written as a helper.

Cast.summon(ref=).why: The verb takes a ref already. All three rows say the blocker is that the spec stripped the printed name so there is no ref to pass -- that is a compendium defect, not an engine gap, and the rule for it is `defect=` / refer up, not a symbol in the queue.

ConditionApplied.cancel.found: c.cancel and the Decision machinery exist; ConditionApplied is a plain Event
ConditionApplied.cancel.why: c.cancel works and ForcedMove is a cancellable Decision -- which is why m1937a3 can write half its trait and not the other half. ConditionApplied is announced after the condition is already on, so there is nothing to refuse; making it a Decision is an engine change with a cascade, not a door.

DamageApplied.from_attack.why: p15844 says it itself: from_attack is already an argument to resolve.deal_damage and simply reaches nothing. The value is in hand at the emit, so this is the one-field widening SurgeSpent got four of at once rather than a missing mechanism.

Despawned.actor.why: World.despawn forgets effects and relations, pops the stores and lifts the body off the grid, and emits no event at all; c.dismiss_companion just calls it. So f3238 has no moment to hang on and no 'before it disappears' to read adjacency at, as it says.

Effect.keywords.why: All three rows assert an Effect carries no keywords -- which keywords_of's own docstring concedes and then answers: the effect's label is the ref of the row that laid it, so the keywords come off the row. feats/general_h.py records f1230, f1241, f1260 and f1328 narrowing 'against charm or fear effects' this way, and i499x1 says the same.

Gear.armour_speed.why: f3140 is right that `Gear` carries the armour as a word and `Movement.speed` never consults it, so there is no speed penalty to waive. Armour penalties exist for skill checks (`skills._armour_penalty`) and nowhere else, so this is the f30 shape: the symbol names the rule whose absence makes the feat free.

Gear.owned.found: engine.actions._picking_up and the `pick_up` action handled at actions.py:1382 (its docstring names cf:swordmage-f0), components.Item.owner, Gear.stowed
Gear.owned.why: Half the marker has landed since it was written: a dropped weapon is an `Item` on the floor that can be picked up, so `c.pick_up()` has a mechanism. Not run down: whether Item.owner plus Gear.stowed is enough for 'owned and elsewhere', which Gear still does not record.

Healed.power.why: Healed carries source, target, amount and hp and no row. i1561x1 confirms the other half is already closed (resolve.heal announces before the hit points go on and amount is writable), so the field is the whole of it -- and the db does carry p1455 for i1561x1, so it is not a ref problem.

Healed.regeneration.why: Healed says who healed whom and how much; nothing marks a tick as a regeneration tick. c.regeneration is written as a TurnStart watcher that heals, so the payout is indistinguishable from any other heal at the event.

Hit.damage.why: DamageApplied carries amount and detail ("what dealt it - a power ref where one did"), and triggers._power_of/by_melee read detail precisely to answer "damages you with a melee attack" - so i2013p1's "carries one and names no power, so it cannot tell a melee attack from a burst" is stale. The heal is half ev.amount off that watch.

Hit.origin.found: dsl.area_of exists but must be handed an origin
Hit.origin.why: Three rows agree independently (m5441a6, m5440a4, i1832x1) and m5441a6 is explicit that its other two markers were wrong while this one is not: Hit carries attacker, target, power, critical, branch and the stamped `among` list, and the square an area was centred on is on no outcome event. c.origin is the asking row's own aim.

Keyword.ALCHEMICAL.why: The engine's Keyword set is closed in types.py and has no alchemical member, so the symbol is literally absent - but c._item_owner names the magic item a row came off, asked of the gear rather than the ref's spelling. I would check whether the item table carries a category that separates a consumable alchemical item from any other item power, which would make the keyword unnecessary.

Keyword.BEAST.why: f3774 says the keyword is outside the closed set, but BEAST_FORM is in the enum (#478) and forms.beast_row gates on it off ctx['power'] for both the attack and the damage context. f3774's own note says the phrase means the druid's shape rows and no companion, which is precisely what beast_row answers.

Keyword.INVIGORATING.found: etl.power._KEYWORDS already extracts the word; Keyword (engine/types.py) has no member; RATTLING is the written pattern
Keyword.INVIGORATING.why: The ETL half is done and the word is dropped at the enum, so nothing in the tree carries or reads it. Cheap, but genuinely absent: RATTLING shows the shape (a word handed to a creature's attacks and asked back), and `c.temp_hp` has no `add=` to raise another row's grant.

Mods.applied().found: Mods.items with .label and .amount(), Mods.total(what, ctx), Mods.split, c.total
Mods.applied().why: `Mods.items` is a plain list whose `label` is the ref of the row that laid each modifier, and `total`/`split` already walk it with a context -- so 'how much did that power put on this roll' is a filter over an existing list, reachable through `c.total`. f1351 still blocks on alignment, which no component carries and this symbol does not name.

SavingThrow.effect.why: _my_save_against_hold matches str(eff) == ev.against over world.effects.of(saver) and then reads eff.conditions, which answers f3751's daze/stun and f3318's condition; keywords_of(label) answers p16001/p16438's charm, fear and psychic ('answerable today, and eighteen rows were carrying SavingThrow.keywords for want of the lookup'), and Effect.ongoing/.source answer f2845's number and f2134's 'your attack'. i3556p1 already ships on this route.

SavingThrow.granted_via.why: 'Which row handed this over' is already carried through a power's use and read by a trigger helper, so the concept exists under the same name. Not run down: the save event carries actor/against/natural/bonus/saved only, so the field has to be threaded through Effects.save -- check whether the feature's own save call can pass it.

SavingThrow.keywords.found: durations.keywords_of(label), and the save context's existing "keywords" key
SavingThrow.keywords.why: durations.keywords_of was written for this exact symbol -- 'eighteen rows were carrying SavingThrow.keywords for want of the lookup' -- and durations.py already computes keywords=keywords_of(eff.label) into the save modifier context about fifteen lines above the emit that builds SavingThrow(against=str(eff)). The effect is in hand at the emit site; the field is one argument away, and nobody has to parse a repr.

SavingThrow.ongoing.why: i3455x1 reports that Effects.save already puts `ongoing` and `dtypes` in the modifier context, so the values exist where the throw is announced and only the event is thin - and c.reroll_save/c.unsave are already on Cast. I would check whether the emit site can carry them, as SurgeSpent's docstring describes doing for four fields at once.

SavingThrow.power.why: f1553 wants a bonus only to saves *its own power granted*, and c.save(on=, bonus=, against=) stamps nothing about the caller -- the event carries actor, against, natural, bonus and saved. Nothing else records who asked for an out-of-turn save, so a standing +1 would pay on every save an ally ever makes.

SkillCheck.target.why: SkillCheck carries actor, skill, bonus, total and success and no subject; six rows across three components each state the same absence independently. Nothing in the corpus ranks above the cut for it.

Target.square.why: Target has creature and object sides and no square side, and dsl._auto_targets resolves to entities; p1217 declares NO_TARGET for the same reason. No candidate expresses a square as an aim point.

TempHP.power.why: events.TempHP carries source, target and amount and no row (events.py:631), and f774 reports resolve.temp_hp consults Mods for nothing, so there is neither a way to tell one pool from another nor a term to add to.

Trigger(SkillChallengeEnded).why: m5581a6 records the check: no `SkillChallenge` class in `engine/events.py` and no such trigger in `vocab.py --brief`. A skill challenge is a narrative structure outside the board, so there is no moment to declare.

TurnStart.initiative.why: There is an event for an initiative check and its docstring says it was announced so a row can answer it, so the moment m3601a6 claims does not exist is on the bus; cover and concealment at that moment are both readable.

Weapon.brutal.why: Brutal N is 'reroll each weapon damage die showing N or less and keep the new face', and that is c.reroll_ones: _rolled_above replaces each die under a floor per die, below= is the exclusive threshold ('3 is the one that says a 1 or a 2'), and keyword=WEAPON narrows it. p15894's 'nothing rerolls a weapon damage die that comes up low' is false. What is still absent is the *column*, so a weapon cannot carry it as a standing property -- and f2099's other half (a group that is not a group).

Weapon.double.found: Weapon.hands == 'double', Gear.weapons (a list), Gear.off, c.w(hand='off'), etl/build.py:305
Weapon.double.why: f951 and f1252 say 'a Weapon has one of each', but the ETL already imports each second head of a double weapon as its own base-weapon row (eleven of the nineteen unpriced ones) and Gear.off plus c.w(hand='off') already roll a second melee weapon's dice -- so the second profile is an extra Weapon in Gear.weapons rather than a new field. Not run down: whether appending one silently makes Gear.two_weapon true, which these cards do not grant.

Weapon.heavy_thrown.why: ability_for resolves Pick.BY_WEAPON with `"heavy thrown" in prop for w in gear.held for prop in w.properties`, so the table does carry the property and f2610's "a printed weapon property the table does not carry" is false; c.wielding(prop) is the door. The row still waits on its second marker, c.trade_accuracy().

Weapon.off_hand_anyway.why: c.counts_as already rewrites what a held weapon satisfies, and weapon_dice mutates the character's own Weapon copies, so per-character weapon rewriting exists. Not run down: counts_as is read only by query.wielding, and Gear.off/two_weapon read properties directly -- would check whether either consults Gear.counts_as.

Weapon.proficiency.found: Gear.weapons is a mutable list of mutable Weapon dataclasses, read live by Cast._wielded/_trained_with/_high_crit
Weapon.proficiency.why: f2405 says 'no way to rewrite the weapon a character is holding ... Weapon is read off the item rather than off the wielder', but proficiency and 'high crit' are read off gear.main at the moment of the attack, so replacing that entry with a dataclasses.replace'd Weapon would say both clauses. Not run down: whether anything caches the wielded weapon, and whether chargen would overwrite it.

Weapon.rusting.found: Weapon.properties -- the field exists, the tag does not
Weapon.rusting.why: properties is an open frozenset[str], so a tag could live there, but nothing in the ETL emits one and the row also needs an item destroyed, which has no verb. Confirmed no candidate in the vocabulary.

World.sunlight.why: A light model does exist -- `query.light_level`, `Grid.light`, `c.unlit` -- so 'the board has no concept of it' is only true of *sunlight* specifically, and `world.terrain` is the set a word like this would live in. Check whether the two rows mean 'bright light' (already askable) or an outdoor-daytime fact nothing sets; `terrain.dress` writes no terrain words at all today.

_note: Verdicts on blocked symbols, so each is judged once. `triage.py` ranks
candidates; a person or an agent decides, and the decision lands here.
mis-marked  the facility exists; the row needs re-pointing or writing
probable    a candidate that looks right and was not run down
real        the gap is real, whatever the ranking suggested
A symbol absent from this file has not been judged. Recording `real` is
as valuable as recording `mis-marked`: it stops the next pass paying to

actions.bluff().why: The check rolls -- f2092 and p16677 both make one -- but actions.legal offers no bluff-for-advantage standard action, so there is nothing to intercept and no beneficiary to redirect.

actions.legal('ready').why: `actions.legal` offers powers, recasts, instinctives, commands, charges, hiding, picking up and spending, and there is no `ready` kind anywhere in the module. m855a2's bonus has no readied attack to sit on because readying is not an action a creature can take.

actions.legal(free_despite_stun=).why: A one-condition waiver already exists and is used by can_react for exactly this printed shape; `legal` calls can_act without it. Not run down: where a per-creature waiver would be stored so legal can read it, and how to limit the carve-out to free-cost actions.

by_ref().found: nothing for these two rows (build._label_refs / _cross_reference_rest exist but did not fire)
by_ref().why: Checked the built item_block specs: i3525x1 carries no power ref at all and i2801p1 carries only cf: class-feature refs, never the channel-divinity row it names. The ETL name-to-ref swap machinery is extensive and works elsewhere, but for these two the name stayed prose, which is the one thing this project may not look up.

c.ability_bonus().why: c.str_mod and its five siblings return self.stats.mod(Ability.X) with no Mods consulted anywhere on the path, so there is no modifier hook to add to -- i2814x1's note is accurate. c.bonus's `what` is attack, damage, save, speed or a defence and refuses anything else.

c.act_after_charge().why: c.extra_action raises the turn's budget and announces ActionGranted, which is the thing m5854a0 wants and which it did not consider - it reasoned only about handing a zeroed slot back. I would check where actions.perform zeroes the slots relative to the charge row's own resolution emit, since the row's objection is purely one of ordering.

c.active_vestige().why: c.build records which leg the warlock took and a labelled c.effect plus c.lingers_label is the general "hold and read arbitrary named state" door, with c.endable for the mid-fight switch. What I could not confirm is where the *set* of two remnants is recorded - that is the same chargen sub-choice shape as chargen.race_choice(), and whether a hold laid at a rest survives into a fight.

c.advantage_on_roll().why: c.gains_advantage lays the attacker-side Mod that query.has_combat_advantage reads, and its sibling c.grants_advantage already has the spend-once machinery, so p11750/p12339 look one `once=` short. f631b and f2468 are a different half - a banked d20 reroll - and would want c.arm_trigger plus keep="best". I would check whether once= can be added to gains_advantage's Mod.

c.alchemical().why: i476x1's 'an alchemical item is not a thing the engine carries' is too strong: the category is a real column, the blocks are declared rows and i3320p1/i3479p1 play, so gating a bonus on ctx['power'] being one of them is reachable. i465p1 is the genuine half -- spending an item needs a consumable inventory, and Gear carries weapons, armour, a shield and a stowed set of weapon refs, nothing else.

c.alignment().why: i3282p1 and f1351 both want 'against evil creatures' and no component records an alignment -- the only occurrence in the ETL is etl/feat._KINDS classifying the *word* in a prerequisite line. f1351 also needs how much a modifier contributed to a roll already made, which is c.amplify_bonus's gap.

c.allies_in_area().why: The attack context carries attacker/target/power and not the area that was struck, so there is nothing to ask who else stands inside a burst. No candidate scored at all.

c.altitude_limit().why: m4737a3 is accurate: `c.hover` holds a creature up and `c.rise` puts it there, and neither refuses to go further. No field caps a height, so there is no half of this row to write.

c.amplify_bonus().why: i1986p1, i2633x1 and f1398 each reach for a modifier *somebody else laid* -- 'both the effect and the size of the penalty are locals in its closure', 'nothing reaches a stored modifier' -- and Mods holds no handle a second row can find. feats.rogue_b.f810 deepens only its own penalty, by re-laying it.

c.area_origin().why: cast_from holds a borrowed origin for a duration and measured_from honours it for ranged, area_burst and wall ranges, with the on-board-and-in-sight proviso -- so i1531p1's burst centred on the struck ally is writable today. Not run down: measured_from skips melee, so check what range kind p11769's stance is about.

c.as_basic(at_will=).why: as_basic files the offer under the window that hands the swing out -- window="ranged" is a granted ranged basic -- and dsl.basic_options drops rows the character does not possess at the moment of the swing rather than at arming. That makes the card's outcome reachable without any interrupt: the at-will is offered in place of the basic before it is declared. f987's docstring already relies on this. _spend_once is the per-encounter limit.

c.as_melee(ref).why: c.as_ranged holds a per-creature, per-duration override of a row's reach and f1239 says the second half (c.as_basic) already works, so the holder for the mirror plausibly exists. I would check whether as_ranged's key can be laid the other way, given its note that it renders "as the distance and nothing else" because _is_ranged reads the printed range line.

c.as_weapon(base=).why: i553p1 says 'the base item is a column and no body swaps it', but a Weapon is built from the weapon table by loader and Gear.weapons is an ordinary list, so taking the other base weapon's dice, reach and group means swapping the entry rather than adding a field. Same unchecked risk as Weapon.proficiency -- whether anything holds the old object.

c.as_weapon(natural=).why: p14205 says 'the bite is a weapon with its own proficiency and damage die and nothing can make one'; as_weapon takes damage=, group=, proficiency=, hands= and properties= and appends the profile to Gear.weapons. What is left is a tag for a natural weapon, not the ability to mint one.

c.attacks_with(ability=).found: c.rolls_with(ref, ability), read by Attack.ability_for before the header
c.attacks_with(ability=).why: `c.rolls_with` exists for exactly this sentence -- 'make a named row attack with a different ability', recorded against the creature because the ability is header data -- and `ability_for` reads it *before* the header. cf:warlord-marshal-f0 refuses on the grounds that `basic.RANGED` fixes the ability in its own header 'where no modifier can reach it', which is the problem `rolls_with` was written to solve.

c.augment_area().why: Targets are chosen before a row's body runs, so a widening applied from inside the body arrives after the area was measured -- the augment cannot reach it. A zone's squares are frozen when laid and a wall's length with them, so the second row has no handle either.

c.augment_free().why: c.spend_points is the only route into an augment and the card pays for one with something else. Nothing else in the corpus scores for it.

c.aura(difficult=).why: The helper's own docstring states the workaround -- 'c.aura has no difficult= of its own ... so the workaround is to create the aura and then flip the field by hand' -- and one row already uses it. Nine rows are marked blocked while a working route sits in the tree.

c.aura(shrinks=).why: resize_aura changes a standing aura's radius in place and announces it, with cap= for a printed ceiling - so "c.aura has no shrinking radius" is stale. m4244a2 stays refused on its compendium.attack_defence defect, which is the real blocker on that card.

c.auto_save(against=).why: That helper watches SavingThrow and sets ev.saved = True for a throw whose `against` carries the printed words, and a live row calls it at armour.py:708. m6671a0's 'there is no verb for forcing one to pass' is stale; for slowing and immobilizing it is better read off the standing effect's conditions, the way items.arms._my_save_against_hold does.

c.bank_reroll().why: Every reroll verb acts on the roll in c.trigger; p16455 needs an unspent reroll held over a window and spent on a later roll, and no component stores one.

c.basic(harmless=).why: `c.basic` delegates to `dsl.use` of whichever row the creature's basic attack actually is, so its damage cannot be suppressed from the caller. i2019p1 also needs one attack roll compared against another, which nothing does, and names `c.cancel` as unavailable because the printed action is a reaction.

c.basic_ability().found: c.rolls_with (read by Attack.ability_for before the header), Powers.basic, Powers.rolls
c.basic_ability().why: rolls_with records the swap against the creature rather than the row, for exactly the reason these rows give, and a basic attack is an ordinary ref held in Powers.basic -- so 'use a different modifier for melee basic attacks' is that call aimed at the creature's own basic row.

c.beast_attacks().why: The clause needs the beast to swing and the companion never takes a turn (#212), so a rider paying out on its hit would be a clause with no case. The row reasons this out and marks rather than writes, which is the right call.

c.become(ref=).why: Nothing swaps which stat block drives a creature mid-fight: c.form changes shape and modifiers, query.stat_block only reads. m1825a3 is refused downstream of m1825a2 for the same reason.

c.best_ability().why: Pick.HIGHEST is documented as the header spelling of "Highest ability modifier vs. Will" and resolves per caster in Attack.ability_for, which also takes a plain tuple and returns max(key=stats.mod) (dsl.py:579). i1066p1's "nothing answers whichever of mine is largest. Fifty-four rows print the phrase" is stale for all of them.

c.blocks_entry().why: Occupancy already refuses both walking and teleporting into a creature's square -- `fits()` rejects an occupied square unless the caller passes `share=True` -- so m6404a1 and m5624a1 both say the printed absolute line adds nothing today. Check whether `c.phasing` or any `share=True` caller can breach it; if not, these rows are writable as confirmations the way `cf:fighter-weaponmaster-f3s0` writes a gate that is false today.

c.blocks_occupancy().why: m6405a1 records its own search ('grep -n "def blocks_occupancy" cast.py' and vocab.py --brief both empty) and the engine agrees: movement._occupied only asks whether the *occupant* shares its space, and c.shares_space grants the opposite. Nothing names a square unenterable against phasing or insubstantial movement.

c.bonus(compute=).why: Mod carries `roll: Callable[[], int] | None`, 'called once per time the modifier is read, which is once per roll'. i1623p1 needs the enemy count recomputed at each swing, which is that callable; c.bonus only exposes it as a `dice` string, so the gap is the Cast door and not the mechanism.

c.bonus(multiply=).why: `c.change_amount(ref, n)` sets a named mechanic's number outright rather than adding, and `c.amount_for(ref, default)` is the read -- which is the shape a doubling needs. Check whether a weapon's two range thresholds can be named mechanics that way; p10744's second half (the weapon is unknown when the stance is taken) looks genuinely open either way.

c.bonus(per_die=).found: nothing (c.change_dice and c.weapon_dice are the near misses the row already ruled out)
c.bonus(per_die=).why: A modifier is laid against a roll's total and nothing scales with how many dice made it, so '-2 to each die of damage' has no hook; f763 and f2766 want the same arithmetic from the other direction. The row's note is the best evidence and it has already been re-aimed twice.

c.bonus(regeneration).why: change_amount is the verb for raising a number another mechanic hands out, and regeneration granted by a named row (p2483, which is declared) is that shape. Not run down: the contract requires the granting row to read amount_for, so p2483 would have to be rewritten -- and this row's other half, Healed.regeneration, is a real gap either way.

c.bonus(retype=).why: Both existing retypes touch the damage a row rolls itself; resolve.deal_damage splits a blow into typed parts and only parts[0] is reachable from the event, so the part a modifier contributed cannot be recoloured. f1639's rider rolls no damage of its own at all.

c.bonus_feat().found: build._named_feats, and the refs are already in data/game.db
c.bonus_feat().why: Queried class_feature: cf:ranger-f0s0's spec now carries f127 and cf:ranger-f0s4's carries f171, both declared rows. build._named_feats' docstring records the fix -- names sitting at the *head* of a run, 'three of them a ranger leg', each granting a feat whose ref already existed. Both markers are stale; write them the way cf:ranger-f0s3 writes f172.

c.boost_attack().why: m1796a3 says 'an attack roll or a saving throw can only be rerolled whole'; c.boost_roll's own docstring is 'add to the triggering roll without rolling it again', and its body handles result.total for attack and ev.bonus/ev.saved for a save. Caveat: boost_roll reads c.trigger, so i1186p1 (a daily minor with no trigger) stays blocked.

c.boost_roll(extra=).why: p6186 reads its die through c.dice_for and hands the skill and which power rolled it over in the context, precisely so a feat can narrow - and f1836 (general_k.py:608) already swaps that die with a gate on the kind of roll. f718's and i2295x1's "+1 to the d6 p6186 itself rolls, only for an arcane/divine power" is the same call with a different die and a different gate.

c.boost_save().why: That helper adds to the announced SavingThrow and rewrites ev.saved ('the total is rewritten here the way SkillCheck is rewritten by c.boost_check') and a live row calls it at waist.py:417 -- which is exactly the twin i1354p1's docstring asks for. m1796a3's attack-roll branch is also stale: c.boost_roll adds to a roll already made (#495).

c.can_hear().why: There is no sound model anywhere: no hearing key beside the darkvision/low_light/blindsight/tremorsense set that query.sees_in reads, and no distance verb for it. All three rows fall back to sight and say so.

c.cannot_act(during=).found: Budget.immediate_round / Budget.opportunity_turn, flipped from a watcher -- m193a3's precedent
c.cannot_act(during=).why: During somebody else's turn the only actions a creature has are immediates and opportunities, and both are gated on those two stamps in Encounter.can_spend; m193a3 already writes one from content. So p16673's bar can be laid by stamping them at the caster's TurnStart and clearing at TurnEnd, which is narrower than dazed or stunned, as the row asks.

c.cannot_attack(opportunity=).why: c.cannot_attack already refuses at AttackDeclared in the BEFORE window, and resolve sets `announced.opportunity = opportunity` on that very event -- _was_opportunity reads it with getattr today. Narrowing is a gate on a flag already on the event the verb reads.

c.cannot_hide().found: nothing (c.no_walk / c.cannot_shift / c.cannot_attack are the precedent family)
c.cannot_hide().why: `actions._hiding` is the single place a hide is offered and it consults only cover, concealment and `hidden_from` -- no effect can refuse one, which is exactly m6644a2's reading that every hide method stops at doing or reading a hide. The verb would be new, though `c.no_walk`/`c.cannot_shift` show the shape.

c.cast_through().why: The engine knows what a power was cast through only for the enhancement bonus it lends. Nothing substitutes a held object's range and proficiency for the power's own, which is the whole of this row.

c.change_distance(ref, n).why: extend_move is literally 'make a named row move you further' keyed by ref, entries add so a negative shortens. Both rows say the hold is that cf:barbarian-f1s3 and cf:rogue-scoundrel-f1s2 hard-code their numbers -- which extend_move's docstring names as the content-side bug ('a row must read it to be changed, with squares_for').

c.charge_at(at=).why: The charge works and square selection exists everywhere else (c.shift(to=), c.teleport(to=), world.reachable_squares), but neither c.charge_at(victim, ref, who) nor c.run_at(victim, who) threads a destination, so nothing today names the walk-in square. Not run down: whether a body can walk by hand and then swing with the charge flag set, which would make this writable without a kwarg.

c.charge_with().why: c.as_basic is "you can use <this row> in place of a melee basic attack" filed under the window that hands the swing out, and "charge" is one of its four windows; actions._charges feeds its swings from basic_options(world, actor, "charge"). So the swap is made before the charge resolves, which is i2088p2's whole objection to c.charge_at.

c.charges().found: Powers.per_day with c.per_day_left / c.spend_per_day, and Powers.used/times(ref)
c.charges().why: i2017p1 says 'an item with a pool of its own is not a thing Magic carries', but a counted, daily-refreshed pool keyed by ref exists and content calls it (features/martial_leaders: 'the gap was the bridge, not the counter'). What I did not run down: whether one pool can be shared by an item's several blocks, and what a non-daily recharge would hang on.

c.choose(before_damage=).why: c.choose exists but is only ever called from inside a body; f1858 needs a question put to the holder at a moment -- before the damage dice are rolled -- that nothing offers. Keyword.RAGE already closed the other half of this row.

c.chosen_weapon_group().found: Build.choices (a free-form set[str]) read by c.build, Gear.counts_as, feats.general_o._group
c.chosen_weapon_group().why: `BuildState.choices` is an extensible string set already carrying `race:<ref>`, `element:<x>` and `primary:<x>`, and `c.build(word)` is a plain membership test -- the same shape as the `race:<ref>` mis-mark already found. Groups are a column `_group` asks about and `Gear.counts_as` already records proficiency waivers, so 'two weapons this character picked' needs a `weapon:<group>` entry, not new machinery.

c.class_feature().found: cf: rows are ordinary @power rows and emit PowerUsed; build._features, build._sub_features
c.class_feature().why: A class feature that has a `cf:` row announces itself like any other row, so the absence is narrower than the symbol: i1942x1/p1's feature has no `cf:` row at all and f3621/f3626/f3645 name features only in prose. Check the same thing `spec.feature_ref()` needs -- which features `etl.build._features` actually imports -- and note that a mid-fight *invocation* of a passive feature has no moment even when the row exists.

c.combined_attack().why: m3842a3 and f3797 both want one attack rolled on behalf of several creatures, with the others paying for it. `c.use_power`, `c.grant_attack` and `c.aid_attack` each move one creature's swing; nothing pools several into a single roll.

c.conceal(from_light=).why: Light is on the board per square and per looker, so reading the square being left and laying a carried `c.conceal(until=)` is writable now; conceal even takes a context predicate. f3067b's 'lighting is not on the board' predates the light model.

c.conjure(defences=).why: Read the body: conjure spawns Ident, Position, Movement and Conjuration and no Health or Defences, so the thing is on the board and targetable but cannot be hit for damage or destroyed. world.spawn takes components, so defences are additive -- what has no precedent at all is m1659a5's other half, routing a hit on the object into a creature's Health.

c.conjure_weapon().why: c.as_weapon grants damage, group, proficiency, properties and hands for a duration and c.conjure makes an entity, so the shape is largely there. What I did not confirm is whether as_weapon can carry the enhancement bonus and critical die p15895 says are the weapon's own columns - if it can, this is one call.

c.considered_bloodied().why: Health.bloodied is a derived property (hp <= max_hp // 2) with no override anywhere, and resolve/query read it directly -- so i691p1's 'bloodied for all purposes without losing hit points' has nothing to pretend with, exactly as it says.

c.consume_item().found: engine/ammunition.py, Item(uses=, spend=), c.give, actions._spending, Ammo.kind
c.consume_item().why: The spend machinery exists end to end: `c.give` spawns a one-shot with charges, `actions._spending` offers it, and ammunition is a modelled consumable whose ref lands on all four attack events. What is missing is that neither `chargen` nor `story` ever deals a character an `Item` or any `Ammo` -- check there before building a verb.

c.counts_as(feat=).why: The existing verb is read by query.wielding and answers only about what is in hand; c.feat(ref) has no writer. m4027a4 also reports its brief names the feat by this row's own ref, so there would be nothing to point a verb at.

c.counts_as(kind=).why: `c.set_origin` writes type/origin words onto a creature as labelled effects that `kinds_of` (and so `c.is_kind`) reads back, and `instead_of=` even takes a word off -- which is most of what f1509/f1511 ask. The residual is that the printed line applies for one attacker only, and writing it globally would be stronger than the card; check whether the origin label can be read through a `when=` gate on the asking row.

c.counts_as(property=).found: c.weapon_dice (writes the per-character `replace(w)` copies in Gear.weapons), feats.fighter_c._with_property, Cast._high_crit
c.counts_as(property=).why: weapon_dice already edits one character's own copy of a weapon and needs no reader, which is the exact mechanism these rows want for `Weapon.properties`; `_high_crit` and `_with_property` already read the field. f1277's three clauses (dice, properties, group, range) are the same write on the same object.

c.cover_from().why: f1296 says 'nothing asks what cover a creature has'. query.cover_between traces it corner to corner at the moment of the attack, and _covering already asks which creature is giving it. What is missing is a Cast door, not a mechanism.

c.crawl().why: MoveStart.kind_ has six words -- walk, shift, teleport, push, pull, slide -- and crawling is not one of them, so there is no half speed to raise and no move to exempt from provoking.

c.crit_damage().found: c.total(what, on, ctx); "crit_damage" is an ordinary Mods key at resolve.py:959
c.crit_damage().why: `resolve.deal_damage` sums the crit rider with `_split_mods(world, source, "crit_damage", dmg_ctx)` -- a normal modifier key -- and `c.total("crit_damage", on=..., ctx=...)` is the general reader for exactly that. i709p1's claim that 'nothing outside that branch can ask for the total' is wrong.

c.curse_damage().why: c.reroll_ones' docstring names "the curse damage" as exactly what its `ref=` narrows to, f2764 says extra_damage reads its die through c.dice_for now, and warlock_f1c11 already pays curse damage inline with c.damage - so f1124/f2036/f2760 are writable today. Only the once-a-round latch is left, and that is c.extra_damage(applies=).

c.damage_disadvantage(against=).why: The rows' stated reason is wrong: c.damage_disadvantage is 'held on the creature that rolls' and takes on=, so it already lands on somebody else. What is genuinely absent is the *attack*-roll twin as a standing modifier -- reroll_attack(keep="worst") only answers a triggering roll. Not run down: whether these two traits are about attack rolls or damage rolls, which decides the verdict outright.

c.damages_with(ref, ability).why: rolls_with is read by Attack.ability_for and never by damage, and the named row works its number out inside its own closure (`c.flat(3 + c.cha_mod, ...)`), so there is nothing for a swap to be read by. The row's own analysis checks out.

c.deals(add=True).why: A blow of several types at once already exists -- c.damage takes dtypes and Mod.dtype is a tuple 'because 1d6 extra cold and lightning damage is one rider of two types' -- and _typed/_retyped is a single read site returning one type. Not run down: whether this card adds a type to the attack's own dice or only to a rider, which decides whether the fix is at _typed or is one c.bonus(dtype=).

c.deals(dtypes=).why: A blow of two types at once is a shape the pipeline very much has: four Cast verbs and the Damage header take dtypes, DamageRolled.dtypes is writable specifically so a listener can say "and" rather than "instead", and p15899 - a neighbour of a waiting row - deals cold and necrotic in one roll. Only the `deals:` label is single-valued.

c.deals(ref=).found: Cast._retyped / Cast._typed, and the c.change_dice / c.change_amount / c.extend_move family
c.deals(ref=).why: _retyped already narrows a 'deals:<type>:<keyword>' override to the row being used -- it reads keywords_of(self._declared()) and skips an effect whose keyword the current row lacks. Adding the ref to that same label and comparing p.ref is the same single read site, and change_dice/change_amount/extend_move are three existing verbs built on exactly this ref-keyed-override contract.

c.deals(when=).why: _retyped walks labelled `deals:` effects and already narrows by keyword, and the damage path carries a context that c.bonus(when=) gates on today (i3169x1 reads ctx target in the same file). So a gate looks like one argument short rather than a missing mechanism; I would check whether _typed's caller has the ctx in hand to pass down.

c.death_save().found: turns._death_saves and items.armour._death_save exist, but neither can be reached
c.death_save().why: A death save is rolled only inside turns._death_saves, on TurnEnd, for a creature holding Condition.DYING -- and loader gives every monster Health(dies_at_zero=True), so m4241a2's target never enters that state. No verb rolls one on demand.

c.death_save_failure().why: i3180x1 says the failure count 'has no counter anywhere'. Health.failures exists, turns.py increments it and kills at three, resolve.py and c.reanimate both reset it. What is missing is a Cast door onto a counter the engine already keeps.

c.death_threshold().why: i1037x1 is accurate: three failed death saves is a literal inside `turns._death_saves`, with no field on the creature for a row to raise.

c.decay(magic=False).why: A mundane weapon has no enhancement for decay to take down, and nothing else records an item as degrading -- so the stacking penalty has no hook and c.destroy has nothing marked to take.

c.defend_with().why: attacks_defence moves attacks onto a different defence, takes on= so it can be laid on the attacker, has from_= to narrow to attacks that started on a named defence, and registers in Window.BEFORE -- which runs after the interrupt window and before roll reads vs, so an interrupt laying it lands in time. Its docstring's own warning applies here: 'the engine has always allowed this and the rows said it did not.'

c.deny_space().why: c.shares_space is the positive operation and has no negative form, and m6407a0's reading is right that the exemptions the card buys - teleport, phasing, two sizes smaller - are what the grid already permits. There is nothing to switch off.

c.difficult_for().why: The per-creature machinery runs one way: World.rough() is the map plus live zones for everybody, and for_ only *removes* squares a creature is exempt from. There is no per-creature addition, which is what m115822a0 and i3436p1 both print. Exempting every other creature from a uniquely-labelled zone is the only route and breaks for anything that arrives later.

c.disable_trap().why: i1371p1 says 'there is no verb for taking one out of action with a check', and every part of that sentence exists separately -- c.douse is the precedent for removing a map feature outright, c.forbid for taking a creature's rows away. Not confirmed: whether a Trap entity can be put out cleanly (it is a creature to the board, not Scenery, so c.douse refuses it).

c.disadvantage(on=).why: damage_disadvantage imposes roll-twice-keep-lower on another creature by laying a 'damage_twice_lower' modifier read inside _roll_damage. The same pattern at the attack-roll site is the whole of f800. Not run down: would check whether resolve.attack has a comparable single read point to consult the key.

c.disarm(catch=).why: `c.disarm` spawns the weapon as an `Item` with `owner=0` in the square, and the existing pick-up path is three lines -- `gear.weapons.append(item.weapon)`, `gear.wield(...)`, `world.despawn(...)`. Catching it is that sequence run by the disarmer instead of the floor; m1819a2/a3 need a kwarg onto code that works.

c.disease_check().why: The state the trait asks after exists, but nothing performs a stage check anywhere: worsen_dc, improve_dc and check_skills appear in no engine or chargen code, and the component's docstring says the stage never advances because an extended rest does not exist. Forcing a check inside a fight has no implementation to borrow.

c.dispel_defence().why: c.dispel destroys a zone or conjuration outright and rolls nothing, so there is no check for the card's bonus to apply to. Nothing in the corpus scores above the cut.

c.double_damage().why: c.bonus adds a number (and dice via dice=), c.maximise takes the ceiling of the roll, and c.reroll_damage rolls twice and keeps the higher. None of the three multiplies a total and nothing else on Cast does.

c.douse_lights().why: Both rows were marked before the light model landed -- m3134a5 says 'c.light() is the reused symbol for the whole gap' and m2515a2 says 'light is not a thing the board holds', while query.light_level now reads Grid.light, dark zones and carried light_radius mods. What I did not run down: any route for a row to darken Grid.light or cancel another creature's carried light.

c.drags_grabbed().why: That helper is exactly this trait: c.watch(Moved, ...) for the whole encounter, sliding every grabbed creature into the square just vacated and laying c.no_provoke per captive. m5481a1 already calls it, so the 'nothing can be hung off a walk' both rows assert is false.

c.draw_card().found: nothing -- and it is a defect as much as a gap
c.draw_card().why: There is no deck model, and all five rows also report that the powers the cards would name were stripped from the spec, so even with a verb there would be no refs to draw. c.draw/draws_free are about weapons and rank only on the word.

c.dying_as().why: resolve applies the dying condition and nothing offers a choice about what comes with it, so rt:r47-t3 has no decision for f1643 to have detected. c.extra_action and Dropped are both already in place; the missing thing is the election.

c.effects_on().found: Effects.of(owner) in durations.py:580, used by c.end_effect, c.suffering, m5746a3
c.effects_on().why: `world.effects.of(eid)` returns every live effect with its label, conditions, duration and ongoing damage, and `c.end_effect` already filters that list by `against=` (label), `carrying=` (condition) and `save_ends=`; m5746a3 reads it inline. p16613 wants to pick a hold and p15931 wants the one imposing a condition -- both are that list plus `c.choose`. Missing a Cast door, not a mechanism.

c.elemental_companion().found: c.summon, c.call_beast -- and neither has anything to summon
c.elemental_companion().why: The summoning machinery exists (c.summon, and cf:ranger-f0 calls c.call_beast), but f3724 records that the spec gives the feat's own id where a creature ref should be, so there is no stat block to put on the board. A data gap under a verb-shaped symbol; the other three rows are all about a companion that is not there.

c.empower(on=ally).why: artificer_empower_reservoir already banks a charge at a rest, spends the day's allowance, and pays c.boost_roll off the holder's own roll with a BANKED_CHARGE_KEY a feat can add to - end to end. The only obstacle is the hardcoded content line `holder = me`; c.choose(c.allies()) and c.held(on=ally) name somebody else's weapon.

c.end_on_attack().why: Both helpers already end a hold on `AttackRolled` -- '"...or until you attack"' -- and f2842's own docstring concedes it, calling this 'the hold ten item blocks carry'. The real hold on f2842 is bolting a sustain clause onto another row's effect, which is a different and genuinely absent thing.

c.exclude_squares().why: An area is a computed square set and nothing punches holes in one, so the squares cannot be left out and the augment has nothing to count.

c.extend_effect().found: powers/druid/level_6_b.p5052 -- effect.when / effect.clock / effect.latch written by hand
c.extend_effect().why: p5052 is a written row whose docstring states the route: 'a zone due to end at the end of this turn is moved onto the end-of-next-turn clock by writing the clock, and latch is what keeps an effect on that clock alive through the turn it was made in'. Effect is a mutable dataclass, so i1960p1/i2762p1/i2323x1/f2628's 'nothing lengthens a live effect' is wrong -- what is missing is a Cast door, as with c.aura(difficult=).

c.extend_move(any_of=).why: The verb exists, takes a context predicate, and its entries add, so 'one more square on every X teleport' is a loop of calls over the enumerable refs rather than a new kwarg. Not run down: extend_move's own docstring warns it is inert on a row that hard-codes its distance, so what to check is whether the affected teleport rows read `squares_for` -- and p12342's extra squares ride a shift granted to the target, with no named row to key on.

c.extend_move(destination=).why: The gate exists but is asked when `squares_for` is read, which is before the destination is chosen, so 'two squares further on any teleport that ends beside X' cannot be asked at the one moment the number is needed. Both rows reached this independently.

c.extend_range().why: _stretched reads Mods.total("range", ctx) for a ranged line and area_of passes ctx={"power": p.ref}, so a named row's range is already lengthenable -- items/weapon_b.py:5043 and powers/paladin/level_7.py:114 both say so in their own docstrings. i2635x1's 'nothing reaches in and lengthens it' is false.

c.extend_reach(ref).why: _stretched reads Mods.total("reach", ctx) for a melee line and area_of passes the row's ref in ctx, so 'stretch one named row's reach' is c.bonus("reach", n, when=lambda ctx: ctx.get("power")==ref) -- feats/druid_b.py:298 and general_o.py:1720 already use the reach modifier. f1985 has the gate solved already, so this closes it.

c.extra_area_target().why: c.add_target appends a creature to the use running underneath an immediate interrupt, and its docstring is explicit that "an appended creature is one that power's body is then called for - attack roll, damage and all". That is widening another row's target line, which is what i1098x1 says nothing does.

c.extra_damage(applies=).found: features/strikers.py:66 (the parameter exists; the latch does not)
c.extra_damage(applies=).why: strikers.extra_damage already takes applies= and per_turn=, and its payout reads a "<label> damage" modifier, so the condition and the size are both reachable - but the latch is a `paid` dict in the closure keyed on round and initiative slot with nothing to clear or bypass. f2076 and i3096x1 each explain why a second watcher pays twice instead.

c.extra_reaction().why: m193a3 writes both printed halves today: c.extra_turn(at=init.rolled + 10) for the second initiative ('ten counts under its own is where the levels below put one') and budget.immediate_round = -1 on TurnStart to hand the immediate action back, because Encounter.can_spend refuses one only while that stamp equals the round. m5719a0 and m1003a6 claim neither can be said.

c.extra_target().found: c.add_target -- only inside a nested use
c.extra_target().why: c.add_target appends to the power 'this one is nested inside' and refuses where nothing is running underneath, which is why f3793 says it 'adds one to the power being cast, not to a power somebody will cast later'. f3304 names the deeper reason: targets are settled before any rider is reached, and the target-settling path reads no per-ref store (unlike Powers.extra_squares, which c.bull_rush does read).

c.extra_turn(script=).found: c.extra_turn -- a whole turn, not one scripted action
c.extra_turn(script=).why: Both rows need one fixed action pinned to an initiative count; extra_turn splices a full turn and hands the policy a free one, which m115683a1 argues is a different creature from the card's.

c.familiar_state().why: Reading the state is done in three places already, so the symbol's own name is not the gap; f2256/f2257 say the gap is that `c.familiar_mode` 'sets one and announces nothing' and that nothing records a destroyed familiar. Check whether a mode change can emit an event the way `c.resize_aura` was given `ZoneResized` for exactly this reason.

c.feats(category=).why: `Power` carries ref, level, cls, usage, keywords and no category, and `etl/feat.py` imports only `tier` (and 664 rows print no tier at all). f2614/f2615's whole payout is the count of feats in one printed family, and no column records family membership.

c.feint().why: There is no feint in the action menu -- no check to put the bonus on and no success to trigger the payout. f2890 notes the payout half alone is writable through the extra_damage key, which is a partial and not the symbol.

c.fell_might().why: features/warlock.py:170 is explicit: "Written, and `c.fell_might()` was never a gap" - the boon is a row with usage=ENCOUNTER so its charge is a use of the feature, and c.expend_row spends one without running it while c.restore_use hands it back. The four waiting rows are reading a note that the feature itself has already retracted.

c.flank_from(square).why: `_flankers_from(c, stand, victim)` answers 'which allies would flank the victim with somebody standing on `stand`' and was 'written against a square rather than against the caster' for precisely this reason. f2609's 'you are considered to occupy that square for flanking' is `grid.flanks` asked from a square, which is already the primitive.

c.flank_from_square().why: Grid.flanks is asked with a bare square against a creature's squares, and _flankers_from was written against a square precisely because its row shifts first and wants to know where to shift to -- which is an empty square standing in for one of the two flankers.

c.flat(unpreventable=).why: No candidate at all. Damage that cannot be prevented or reduced has no reader anywhere.

c.floating_object().found: c.conjure (returns an entity id with a Position), movement.place
c.floating_object().why: conjure already puts a positioned, drawable, targetable thing on the board and returns its id, which is the 'object somewhere' this row says does not exist. Not run down: there is no swap-places verb, so the exchange would be hand-written from the two positions, and i3221p2 is a teleportation card where that may matter.

c.floor_damage_dice().found: Cast._rolled_above and Cast._reroll_floor inside Cast._roll_damage, c.reroll_ones(below=)
c.floor_damage_dice().why: The dice are in hand in `_roll_damage` -- `_rolled_above` already replaces each die under a floor, one at a time, keeping the faces that came up fine -- so 'the dice are gone' is what reroll_ones' own docstring refutes. 'Treat a 1 or 2 as a 3' is the same hook taking max(face, floor) instead of rerolling.

c.forces(target=).why: The shove builds `ctx = {"how": how.value, "power": power}` and reads ev.target eight lines later for the resist side, so the victim's eid is in hand at the gate; and c.bonus gates already read ctx.get("target") in the damage path (f1863, i3169x1 in the same file as a waiting row). One key in a dict that already exists.

c.forgo_attack().why: That pair is this project's mechanism for a standing registration that is 'offered, never imposed' at a named row's clause, which is the shape of 'withdraw the second attack to stay hidden'. Not run down: it only fires if the swinging row itself calls c.instead_of at that clause, and I did not check the two-attack row in question. f1296's other half, cover, is already mis-marked in the fixture.

c.forgo_damage().found: c.pre_empt + c.instead_of, c.reduce, DamageRolled as a Decision
c.forgo_damage().why: f2428's own docstring says `DamageRolled` 'is a `Decision` whose `amount` a listener may write', and `c.reduce(amount, ev)` writes it; `c.pre_empt(ref, what, clause)`/`c.instead_of(what, default)` is the general mechanism for one row replacing a *named clause* of another, with `c.may` for the choice. Giving up all of a blow is therefore sayable today -- only f2428's 'take one die out of a folded total' is not.

c.forgo_healing().found: Cast.half_healing (Healed, Window.BEFORE, mutates ev.amount), resolve.spend_surge (SurgeSpent is a Decision; c.no_surges refuses one)
c.forgo_healing().why: `Healed` is negotiable before it applies -- half_healing halves the amount that way rather than clawing it back -- and a surge spend is refusable, so refusing the hit points a second wind puts back is writable today. Only f2005's half is different: suppressing one clause of another row's body is not a healing question.

c.forgo_save().why: c.save picks the first save-ends effect and rolls; SavingThrow is announced only in the bare branch and the caller ignores `cancelled`, so no interrupt could decline it. c.unsave fails a save that is happening, which spends the chance instead of keeping it.

c.forgo_teleport().found: c.pre_empt(ref, what, clause) + c.instead_of(what, default), c.substitutions
c.forgo_teleport().why: f2699 refuses because 'a clause of another row cannot be suppressed', but `pre_empt`/`instead_of` is the general clause-substitution mechanism -- one row registers a replacement against another row's named clause and `dsl.use` offers it as a variant. The thin part is that the teleporting row must call `c.instead_of("teleport", ...)`, which is a content edit.

c.form(class_form=).why: The keyword landed but every power printing it is above the imported tier, so there is no form anything can enter and no state to gate on. `todo=` rather than `dropped=` is right: there is no payout to withhold.

c.form(mimics=).why: c.in_form answers which shape, and the row correctly rules it out: what is needed is whether the shape is *that particular creature's*, which c.form cannot be told and nothing records. The naming half is already closed (p2472 is declared).

c.grab(attackable=).why: A grab is a relation between two entities (Relation.GRABBED_BY, c.grab(by=)) and nothing makes a limb an attackable thing with its own defences. m3300a3 says it checked this against cast.py, and the cap it also needed already works without this row.

c.grab(bonus=).why: i1468x1 says 'c.grab simply takes hold -- there is no roll for a modifier to reach', but c.grab_attempt rolls Strength vs Reflex with as_='grab' and as_ rides the attack ctx; c.bull_rush's docstring records that 14 modifiers already gate on the same key.

c.grab_reach().why: Relation.GRABBED_BY means adjacent and nothing else, so a hold that reaches two squares has no expression. (m5648a3's docstring also claims c.grab takes no dc, which its own body contradicts with dc=13 -- a separate stale note.)

c.grabbing(auto_share=).why: m6113a0 is accurate: `share=True` already drags a grabbed creature along for one call, and nothing makes every future move do it without being told. The standing licence would be a movement-layer flag that does not exist, and the printed check has no grab check in this tree to modify.

c.grant_action('mount').why: c.grant_action's docstring prescribes exactly this work: 'anything else is carried, costs nothing and does nothing, so add the reader in actions at the same time as the word'. actions.legal already does it for stand (reading _granted for the cheaper cost), and c.ride is the payload. A word plus a menu reader, not a mechanism.

c.grant_action(charge).found: c.grant_action (its own docstring: 'anything else is carried, costs nothing and does nothing, so add the reader in actions at the same time as the word'), actions._charges, c.charge_at
c.grant_action(charge).why: The charge exists twice over -- as an action menu entry and as a verb -- so the word only needs the reader the verb's docstring already prescribes. This is the thin door onto something that works, not a mechanism.

c.grant_action(familiar=).why: The same documented extension point as c.grant_action('mount'): add the word and its reader in actions, which legal already does for stand. c.move_companion is the payload and works. One word and one menu branch.

c.grant_action(standard).why: c.extra_action "drops one action into the budget the turn is already spending, which Encounter.can reads back", takes any ActionType and an on=, and announces ActionGranted - whose docstring calls Cast.extra_action "the one door". m4488a2's and m5460a4's "takes a standard action" is c.extra_action(ActionType.STANDARD); c.grant_action's closed four-word list was the wrong verb to look at.

c.grant_armor().found: nothing (c.as_weapon is the analogue, with no mirror)
c.grant_armor().why: c.as_weapon exists for the weapon side of the same sentence and there is no armour equivalent - nothing puts a worn item on a creature mid-fight, so an enhancement bonus and the item's columns have nowhere to live. p16411 names c.grant_weapon() as the sibling marker group.

c.grant_inline().found: a coined ref plus c.grant_row -- the f1253/f1253b and rt:/cf: precedent
c.grant_inline().why: i1188p1 and i2980p1 both say the granted power 'has no ref of its own'. Content coins refs routinely for rows the compendium does not number (f1253b via _swap, every rt: and cf:), the author has the card's full text in the brief, and c.grant_row then hands the declared row over -- so these are rows to write rather than a facility to build.

c.grant_trait(mount).why: m3288a8 says 'nothing on the board records that one creature is riding another'. Relation.RIDDEN_BY does, and c.mount() returns the ridden creature -- m4027a4's docstring states it outright ('the mount half needs nothing new -- c.ride, c.mount and c.rider already exist'). The trait is c.ignores_difficult(on=c.mount()).

c.grant_weapon().why: i1261x1 says 'nothing adds one to Gear.weapons from a body'; as_weapon builds a Weapon and appends it to Gear.weapons, stowed so actions._wielding offers the draw. Armour-that-is-also-a-weapon is the same shape as the shield-as-weapon the verb was written for.

c.guild_training().why: i998x1 adds to the temporary hit points a named class feature hands out, and nothing models that feature or announces its payout -- the same family as `c.class_feature()` and with the same root: the feature has no row.

c.heal_check().found: engine.skills ('heal' is a skill), c.check, events.SkillCheck
c.heal_check().why: The check rolls, but no action offers one in a fight so no SkillCheck with that skill is ever announced, and the event names an actor with no patient -- which is the half both rows need to tie the check to whoever was healed.

c.healing_infusion().found: cf:artificer-f2 and p4128 / p7635 / p10187, all declared
c.healing_infusion().why: Checked the registry and the item spec: cf:artificer-f2 is declared, the item's own spec names it by ref, and the three infusion cards it budgets are all declared too -- so 'one named class feature nothing models' is false and PowerUsed on those three refs is the window. Not run down: I did not read the card's payload clause, so I cannot say the whole row is writable.

c.hide(auto=).why: The worked pattern is in the tree twice: query.cover_between decides whether the creature has cover or concealment and c.hide() follows, which is the accepted simplification given no opposed Stealth roll exists. c.arm_trigger is what arms a standing permission that costs the watcher the action, which is m6344a0's stated objection.

c.hide(cover=).found: query.cover_between answers the cover half; nothing models a hide *attempt*
c.hide(cover=).why: c.hide delegates straight to c.invisible and grants the state outright, so cf:rogue-scoundrel-f1s2's 'permission to attempt a hide' has nothing to attempt: there is no Stealth-versus-Perception contest in skills.py, and granting the state on MoveEnd would be strictly stronger than the card, as the row says.

c.hide(despite_cover=).why: Hiddenness is the HIDDEN_FROM relation and the loss of cover ends it with nothing holding it open; the row was already re-pointed once off c.stay_hidden() after that need turned out to be a window instead. No candidate scored.

c.hit_count().why: `_hits_this_use` counts 'how many of this row's targets it has hit on this use' by walking the bus back to this row's own `PowerUsed` -- the count the symbol names, already written. f1123 keeps a separate residual the symbol does not name: the first target's damage is paid before the second hit is known, so the bonus has to be applied retroactively.

c.hit_twice().why: 'The one creature a resolved use hit with two separate attacks' is written and answers off PowerResolved.rolls, so a single use's second hit is askable. Not run down: i2981p1 may mean two hits across different uses -- check whether its printed trigger is one use or an encounter tally, which _twice cannot see.

c.ignore_concealment().why: f1832 already corrected itself -- 'c.ignore_cover does waive the concealment -2 ... so the verb is not absent' -- so m5427a0's 'nothing reads a concealment exemption' is wrong. But cover and concealment share one Mods key and cover_waived takes the larger of two, so writing either row with the existing verb is strictly stronger than its card. What I would check: whether splitting the key into a concealment-only one is local to cover_waived and cover_between.

c.ignore_condition(redirect=).why: Both halves exist: ignore_condition suppresses a standing daze or stun without curing it, and grant_attack makes a named creature swing now at a named target. ConditionApplied announces after the condition lands, which suppression tolerates. Not run down: whether the printed 'instead' tolerates a suppress-then-force sequence, and whether the attack must be the creature's own choice (c.dominate) rather than aimed.

c.ignore_cover(concealment_only=True).why: resolve.situational takes the larger of cover and concealment and consults one waiver for the pair, so there is no concealment-only half to turn off. Both rows ran this down and refused to lay the broad waiver, which would let the creature shoot through a wall.

c.ignore_cover(reroll=).why: f2849's reasoning holds: c.ignore_cover takes a when= gate, but cover is read inside defence() with resolve's own context where reroll is always False, and the reroll's context exists only for the attack re-sum. A gate on it would be silently false rather than wrong.

c.ignore_hazards().why: m6073a0: c.resist and c.immune are about an attack's damage types and about conditions; a zone's burn and a hazard's damage reach the creature through Effect.ongoing and the zone's own tick, and nothing waives either by source.

c.ignore_line_of_effect().found: query.line_of_effect -- the check, not a waiver
c.ignore_line_of_effect().why: line_of_effect is consulted in targeting and nothing sets it aside; c.ignore_cover is the analogous waiver and covers cover and concealment only. The read exists and the override does not.

c.ignore_requirement(ref).found: nothing (c.waive is conditions, c.counts_as is weapon requirements only)
c.ignore_requirement(ref).why: f2933 is right that the gate is asked by `dsl.usable` off the header before any body runs. `c.counts_as` relaxes a *weapon* Requirement through `Gear.counts_as` and `c.waive` relaxes a condition's costs; neither reaches a row's printed Requirement predicate, and nothing standing on a creature does.

c.ignores_charge_lockout().found: components.Budget, content precedent writing Budget by hand (powers/battlemind/level_7)
c.ignores_charge_lockout().why: actions.py zeroes standard, move and minor unconditionally after a charge, but content does reach Budget directly, so restoring them from a watcher may be available. Not run down: the ordering -- whether a row's watcher can fire after actions.py has zeroed the budget.

c.ignores_difficult(in_light=).found: nothing -- Movement.ignores is a label set
c.ignores_difficult(in_light=).why: The light half is already readable (c.unlit), so the symbol is squarely the gated ignore, and Movement.ignores is a set of strings with nowhere to hang a predicate while when= is the convention on every modifier verb. The row says 33 rows want this kwarg, which makes it the largest single one in the tree rather than a mis-mark.

c.ignores_difficult(squares=).why: c.ignores_difficult is a set of terrain labels with a when= word, so it is all-or-nothing by construction and there is nowhere to put a count. f1873 writes the charge half exactly and explains why the partial half is a different gap.

c.ignores_difficult_in(who=).found: c.ignores_difficult(kind=, on=) keyed to the zone's own difficult label
c.ignores_difficult_in(who=).why: Zone.difficult may be a *string* and Zones.difficult_squares hands that label through as the terrain kind, while c.ignores_difficult takes both a kind and a creature -- so a single named enemy can be exempted from exactly one zone's ground, which is p16064's 'enemies that lack earth walk'. f1341 wants the inverse (one enemy affected, everybody else not) and that still means exempting the rest of the board.

c.immediate_actions().why: Nothing grants a second immediate action, and m3471a4 needs one scoped to a single named row. No candidate came near.

c.immune(vs=).why: m5789a0 wants 'takes damage as normal but ignores all other effects' of attacks against one defence. Scoping a *defence bonus* by attack kind is routine (items.arms._vs_ranged), but a rider is applied by the attacking row's own body right after `c.hit()`, so there is nothing to intercept.

c.immune_power().found: c.forbid (takes a row away from its owner), c.immune (conditions), c.resist (damage types)
c.immune_power().why: Nothing asks 'is this creature immune to the row being used on it', and neither immunity verb takes a ref -- forbid is about the holder of a row, not its target. The temp-hp conversion needs the same absent hook.

c.improvised().why: There is no improvised weapon row in the weapon table, so the proficiency header has no ref to name and the 1d8/1d10-plus-2 line has no weapon to sit on. A data gap, and cf:fighter-weaponmaster-f3s0 names it as one of three separate holds.

c.in_vehicle().why: Nothing puts a creature inside another one - c.shares_space covers only the square, c.ride/c.mount covers only a rider - so there is no place for the interior, the doors that cut line of sight, or the occupants who move with it. Three rows on one creature wait on it.

c.in_zone(label=).found: World.zones.all() -> zone.label / zone.owner / zone.squares; powers.warden.zone_named, level_11 _labelled_squares
c.in_zone(label=).why: m3828a4 says 'nothing can ask whether a creature is standing in somebody else's zone', but zones are enumerable with their owner, label and squares, and powers/druid/level_6_b.p5052 already walks world.zones.all() and reads zone.squares on a written row. The gate is a membership test over that, not a missing mechanism.

c.initiative_bonus().why: i1970x1 says 'a trait is armed after the rolls, so there is no way to add to the check'. adjust_initiative handles exactly that case -- its comment says `started` is set after _arm_traits, so a trait bumping the number now re-splices the order -- and lint.py already names c.initiative(amount, on=) as the replacement for the unread 'initiative' modifier key.

c.installed(ref).why: m5641a2's Requirement is that a named installation off the board is running; `c.scenery` is map furniture inside the fight and `c.terrain` is what sort of place it is, and nothing holds a standing off-board arrangement.

c.insubstantial(when=).why: i2426x1 refuses on the grounds that 'the damage context carries no attacker', which is stale: `dmg_ctx` has carried `source` and `from_attack` since #302, and `_scoped_vuln` already reads a predicate-gated defence off `vulnerable_when`. `insubstantial`'s own `except_`/`half_except` is where a `when` would hang, beside the halving that is read inside the same context.

c.invisible(when=).why: A re-asked, per-looker gate exists for concealment -- conceal takes a context predicate and total concealment is already aimed at one named creature -- so the distance and daze gates may be sayable that way. Not run down: whether these cards need HIDDEN_FROM's extra effects (targeting, combat advantage), because that is a relation and cannot carry a gate.

c.item_charges().why: A ref-keyed counted resource with a spend and a query already exists and is the shape charges are -- Powers.per_day is a dict of ref to count. Not run down: charges have no daily reset and no printed maximum anywhere on Item, so the clock and the ceiling are genuinely absent even though the counter is not.

c.item_set().why: The module says the 15 set pages' tables 'are not theirs and are not read here at all', and each member is parsed as a separate Item row, so no set membership reaches the database. Nothing to count and nothing to ask after.

c.jump(no_provoke=).found: c.no_provoke(when=) with the opening's kind and mode
c.jump(no_provoke=).why: The no_provoke gate is read inside the veto and is handed "how and by what means the provoker moved" alongside actor/provoker/why (cast.py:4643), so a narrowing by kind of movement is already sayable. The obstacle is that c.jump delegates straight to c.move, so the step reads as a walk; I would check whether a jump can carry its own kind through movement.

c.lend_augment(ref_or_class, clause).found: c.lend_augment(ref, cost, clause) -- the verb exists
c.lend_augment(ref_or_class, clause).why: f3170 wants to hand p10440 an Augment 1 clause it does not print, and that is the verb's stated purpose: 'Four feats print an Augment line on a card that prints none'. The marker's 'ref_or_class' asks for a whole class of rows where the row names one ref. The real proviso is the verb's own: the lent-to row must ask with augment.lent(c).

c.lend_defences().found: c.rider()/c.mount() close the other half only
c.lend_defences().why: Finding the rider is solved; substituting one creature's defence numbers for another's is not, and 'not including any temporary bonuses' rules out computing a difference and laying it as a modifier.

c.lend_skills().why: `c.passive(skill, of=other)` reads another creature's modifier (plus 10) and `c.bonus("skill:insight", 2)` is a live key -- cf:ardent-f0 lays one -- so 'use my modifier for these four skills' is the difference of the two laid as four modifiers. f30 is writable today; nothing new is needed.

c.light(square=).why: m4589a3 refuses because 'the engine has no light level', which is stale: `c.light` lays a carried `light_radius`, `query.light_level` is the reader and `Grid.light` is the painted map field (query.Light: 'absent from Grid.light means BRIGHT'). Lighting a square rather than a creature is a kwarg onto an existing model.

c.line_of_sight_from().why: measured_from traces line of sight and effect from a lender's square for ranged, area_burst and wall ranges while the lender is on the board and in sight, and cast_from holds that for a duration -- so 'nothing can move where it looks from' is no longer true.

c.make_critical().why: That helper writes the critical onto the live AttackResult inside the Hit interrupt window *and* onto the event, precisely because the outcome is recomputed from the result object -- so promoting a swing is done in the tree today. f976's remaining difficulty is its own: two swings come out of one row in an order it cannot pin down, which is an ordering problem rather than a missing facility.

c.make_thrown().why: c.as_ranged's body is one call: self.bonus("reach", max(0, squares_-1), when=lambda ctx: ctx.get("kind","melee")=="melee", once=True, stacks=False). The standing weapon property these rows want is the same modifier without once=True, so what is missing is a kwarg on an existing verb, not a mechanism. It carries the same approximation as_ranged already ships and documents (distance only, no cover or opening change).

c.mark_penalty().why: change_amount exists for precisely this sentence -- 'the size of what a mechanic grants is written inside its own body, so "you grant a +3 bonus, rather than the normal +2" had nothing to change' -- and it is how MANOEUVRE_AID is raised by seven rows. _mark_penalty returning a hard-coded 2 is the shape change_amount's docstring calls this component's commonest bug; make it read amount_for and all four rows become 'instead' rather than 'as well'.

c.max_height().why: c.height reads the distance and c.rise/c.hover set it, and nothing caps it - c.leash bounds distance from a creature or a square, not altitude. m115827a0's whole printed trait is the cap.

c.max_hp().why: f171 and f3313 both want a character's maximum raised and Health.max_hp is written only by loader and chargen -- there is no mod key for it and no content row touches it (surge_value and bloodied are derived from it, so a per-encounter hand-flip would also creep). A build-time grant, like the chargen.* symbols already judged real.

c.max_surges().why: components.py:132 holds max_surges, turns.py:704 refills to it, and a content row already writes `health.max_surges += 1` by hand in feats/paladin.py. The pool is raised and honoured; what is absent is a Cast door, which items/waist.py:848 already says in so many words.

c.maximise(dice=).why: f3610 says the listener reads damage_of(0), finds nothing and returns -- true of the DamageRolled listener and only that. c.maximise also lays a `maximise` Mod, and _roll_damage consults _take_maximum() where 'the dice are in hand', written precisely because a character's damage is rolled in the body.

c.milestone().why: The place a milestone count would live exists -- `Sheet` even comments that 'a milestone grants more' action points -- but nothing counts encounters within a day: there is no encounter counter in `story`, and `LongRested` is defined in `events.py` and never emitted. cf:artificer-f0 under-grants deliberately for this reason.

c.min_die().found: Cast._rolled_above, Cast._reroll_floor, c.reroll_ones(below=), all inside Cast._roll_damage
c.min_die().why: A floor under each individual die is exactly what `_rolled_above` applies, per die rather than per expression, where the dice are in hand -- the same place c.maximise and reroll_damage are read. The row's premise that the dice are gone by the time anything looks is wrong.

c.modify_power().why: Swapping one condition for another inside another row's zone needs a hold on that row's body, and the ref-keyed override family (change_dice, change_amount, extend_move) all require the target row to read the modifier -- there is no route that edits a row from outside it.

c.move(through=).why: _through_them covers a stated number of squares straight through whoever is in the way, reporting each creature entered once, by calling movement.overrun with the printed kind - and c.shift(share=)/c.teleport(share=) do the single occupied square. So "entering an occupied square has no verb" is stale on both counts.

c.move_through().why: `_through_them` covers a stated distance straight through whoever is in the way and calls movement.overrun with the printed kind, reporting each creature entered once. p16677's rider is that call. m5431a1's residue -- squeezing through an aperture -- is a grid gap and a different symbol.

c.move_through_enemies().why: level_01/skirmishers_sa._shift_through states it outright: "'It can move through enemies' spaces' is share=True on the step rather than a waiver of anything", and level_11/skirmishers_sc._through_them covers a run straight through bodies via movement.overrun. i3441x1's 'c.phasing goes through walls, not through people' is looking at the wrong verb.

c.movement_tax().why: Difficult terrain is a property of a square - c.zone(difficult=) and the terrain label set - and nothing charges by direction of travel or by proximity to a particular creature. All three rows reach that conclusion independently and c.slowed is the only near thing, which caps a whole move.

c.next_attack_becomes().why: i2452p1 and i1440p1 both name c.deals as 'the nearest thing' and say the only thing stopping it is that Cast._typed applies the override to weapon powers alone, so an arcane implement row is untouched. The override store and its reader exist; what I did not confirm is whether that weapon-power test is the single gate, or whether an implement row's damage is rolled somewhere _retyped is never consulted.

c.no_coup_de_grace().why: c.coup_de_grace consults nothing on its victim, so there is no exemption to set; i2163x1's other clause is out of combat entirely.

c.no_encounter_attacks().why: `_no_limited_attacks` already writes 'cannot use daily or encounter powers' by walking `Powers.all` and calling `c.forbid` on every non-at-will row with an attack line, ending them all off one save-ends hold. cf:assassin-f1s1 refuses on the grounds that the set would be 'a hand-listed set of refs that goes stale' -- `_arcane_rows` shows the registry filter is the answer instead.
