c.no_enter(zone).found: nothing -- `no_enter` exists nowhere in the engine, only in these two content markers; Zone carries difficult, blocks_sight and obscured and no exemption
c.no_enter(zone).why: The row's premise is wrong in the harder direction: nothing bars a creature from entering a square or a zone at all, so 'except its owner' is not the missing half. Both rows need the bar itself built first.

c.no_miss_damage(half=).why: deal_damage is handed a miss flag and keeps it out of the damage context, and c.no_miss_damage's docstring confirms it is 'the only thing that reads it'. Halving needs the flag where a gate can see it, which is a small engine change and not an existing facility.

c.no_teleport().why: c.forbid's own docstring names this sentence: 'p12344's "cannot teleport" is the same sentence about a different keyword', and it takes both keyword= and lacking=, which is i2908p1's 'in both directions'. c.no_walk is the mode-barring mirror and is three lines -- a Mods key plus a reader in query.can_walk.

c.obscure(level=).found: c.conceal(total=) -- the grades exist, the step-down does not
c.obscure(level=).why: conceal lays a kind='concealment' modifier at 5 (total) or 2 (partial) where the larger wins, so laying a 2 over a standing 5 changes nothing. Downgrading a concealment already in force has no expression in either the modifier path or Zone.obscured.

c.on_aegis().found: c.use_power / c.grant_row as the announcing door
c.on_aegis().why: The blocker f1156 names is purely that the three aegis rows roll their punishment inside a closure the minor-action body arms, so nothing distinguishable is emitted - and a punishment written as its own row would announce PowerUsed. That is a content restructure rather than an engine gap; I would check whether an aegis punishment can be split out without changing what it does.

c.on_any_sustain().found: c.on_sustain(effect, fn) takes any Effect; World.effects.of(who) hands the live ones back
c.on_any_sustain().why: i2900x1 says c.on_sustain only answers 'an effect this row made', but the verb takes an Effect object and appends to its on_sustain list, so another row's live hold can be bolted onto. Not run down: there is no Sustained event, so effects laid *after* the item's property arms would be missed -- which may be the whole of what the card means.

c.on_damage_die().why: DamageRolled carries a total and _roll_damage returns a sum, so the individual faces exist nowhere a row can read.

c.on_damage_reduced().why: i1834x1 is accurate: `c.reduce` takes the number off the damage and emits no event of its own, so there is no moment for a second row to answer. `DamageRolled`/`DamageApplied` announce the roll and the application, never a reduction.

c.on_defiling().why: Nothing in the vocabulary comes close, and the three feats record that the ability the clause rides on is in no compendium table at all -- no Power, Feat, Theme or Class -- so there is no ref to watch and no event to hook. f3190 reached this after already being re-aimed off c.class_feature().

c.on_dismiss(ref, fn).why: `c._banish` despawns a conjuration silently and `events.py` has `Summoned` and `ZoneEnded` but no dismissal event; f3189/f3200 both say the payout of a deliberate end is `c.endable(then=)`, which a row writes into its own body and a second row cannot add to.

c.on_extra_damage().why: That helper *arms* a once-per-round rider. f1114 needs a rider's payout *announced*, so an area power can copy the amount onto its other targets. The writer exists and the event does not.

c.on_feature_power().why: c.pre_empt(ref, what, clause) names a clause *inside* a row - "pull", "temp_hp", "fell_might_damage" - and hands the substitute the same Cast, which is the nearest thing in the tree to reaching a feature's internal moment. I would check whether a registered clause can run instead_of's default and add to it (riding rather than replacing), which is what f788 and f469 need.

c.on_feature_roll().why: The feature is modelled and the replacement is sayable, but the die is rolled while the trait arms and announced to nobody, so the call can only be made once the answer is known -- which would make the choice free. The missing thing is the moment, and nothing stands in for it.

c.on_flanked().why: _enemy_flanked_me is a Trigger(Moved, ...) predicate reading team, distance_between and flanked_by -- 'an enemy ends its movement in a square where it flanks it' -- and a second monster block does the same on MoveEnd. f1282b's 'nothing announces the moment it becomes true' is false; the window is a Moved watcher, and its Effect half (c.no_advantage) is already writable.

c.on_grab_attack().found: c.grab_attempt + as_="grab" on the attack events and the damage/attack ctx
c.on_grab_attack().why: c.grab_attempt rolls Strength vs Reflex with as_='grab' (#501, #510), and resolve stamps as_ into the attack ctx and onto AttackDeclared/AttackRolled/Hit -- c.bull_rush's docstring says 'as_="bull_rush" is what the 14 modifiers gate on'. So i774x1's 'a grab is an ordinary attack the engine does not label' and f2427's 'there is no roll to crit with' are both stale. m4388a3 (a bonus to dragging a held creature) is a separate manoeuvre with no as_ of its own.

c.on_granted_shift().why: MoveEnd carries actor, at and kind_ and no power (events.py:182), and f469 reports the same for Forced - so nothing says which row granted a step. query.granted_actions answers what a creature *may* do, not what a row just caused.

c.on_instinctive().found: as_= on c.attack (the grab/bull-rush label), actions._instinctives
c.on_instinctive().why: f1876 says the attack a summon makes on its own 'is announced as an ordinary attack by an ordinary creature'. The engine already has a label that rides the attack events and the ctx for exactly this kind of narrowing, and the action kind 'instinctive' exists in actions.py. Not confirmed: whether the instinctive path can thread as_ through to the summon's own attack call.

c.on_invisible().why: c.hide calls c.invisible on the same HIDDEN_FROM relation with the same label, so one event cannot say which happened and a row firing on it would answer by hiding again. The moment is the gap, not the mechanism.

c.on_invoke_shrouds().why: f3636 is accurate: `c.spend_shrouds` clears the whole count in one step and emits nothing, so 'they are not removed' has no moment to answer. `c.shroud`/`c.shrouds` read and lay them but announce no invocation.

c.on_miss_all().why: 'Every roll this use made came up short' is answerable off PowerResolved and is written three times over, so f2448's 'Miss is announced per target so it cannot be asked' is stale. Its residue -- a reroll from PowerResolved buying nothing -- is c.reroll_attack(rolls=)'s symbol, not this one.

c.on_pact_boon().found: triggers.cursed_by_me + events.Dropped, as used by features/warlock.py (cf:warlock-f1s4)
c.on_pact_boon().why: Every pact boon is a row declared `on=Trigger(Dropped, cursed_by_me, ...)` and warlock.py says 'the boons are already paid', so the moment a boon triggers is that pair of facts. cf:warlock-f1s4 already writes the printed sentence 'when your pact boon triggers' as `c.watch(Dropped, fell)` guarded by `cursed_by_me`.

c.on_points_spent().found: c.spend_points (records the spend against the row's ref), powers.augment.spent_on
c.on_points_spent().why: The spend is recorded in PowerPoints and announced only as a `Note`, so a pool reaching zero is on nobody's bus. f3322's other half is a declared `out_of_combat` trait, which is inert by design rather than missing.

c.on_power_bonus().why: Mods records a modifier's number and kind and not the act of laying one, so a bonus being granted announces nothing a row can answer. f2074's second hold (which shield) is separate and also open.

c.on_racial_bonus().found: Mods entries carry m.kind, and "racial" is a kind in use
c.on_racial_bonus().why: Mods.total buckets by kind and takes the larger of each (components.py:626), and content lays kind="racial" bonuses today (f3214), so the number exists per kind and only a read-by-kind door is absent - which would answer f3787. I would check that the racial rows actually tag their bonuses; f1863's half is a prose trait with no row either way.

c.on_racial_power().found: c.expend_row + c.restore_use, and f2830 is this row already written
c.on_racial_power().why: The _racial helper's own text says the hold is that 'the racial power is named in prose with no ref', and f2817's note says 'c.expend_row is the spending and c.restore_use is the payout, so f2830 next door is this row written out'. No hook is missing; the brief's missing ref is, which is c.race_option()'s family and build._racial_powers' territory.

c.on_reduce().found: c.reduce -- the act, with no announcement
c.on_reduce().why: c.reduce takes a number off a rolled DamageRolled and emits nothing, and the creature the payout is owed to is known only inside that callback.

c.on_return_to_play().why: f3578 is accurate: a creature that leaves the board and comes back does so through `World.spawn`, which emits `Summoned` only for a summon. Out-of-play rows exist (feats.general_u._f3463_vanish) but none announces the return.

c.on_sanction().why: The event names the relation and the two creatures and not the row that set it, and every class's mark is the same relation value, so there is no way to tell which mark just landed. Nothing else announces a mark.

c.on_save().found: Trigger(SavingThrow, pred) -- items.arms.i3556p1 ships on it
c.on_save().why: i1516x1 itself says 'SavingThrow is announced before it is acted on, so the roll itself is reachable from a c.watch' and asks only for the hook plus a gate; the hook exists as a declared Trigger and i3556p1 uses it with a predicate. The gates split: f3318's condition is answerable off the standing effect (see SavingThrow.effect), i1516x1's 'which row granted the bonus' is SavingThrow.power and real, and f3470's save-against-prone is a moment that never happens.

c.on_sustain(group=).why: c.on_sustain(effect, fn) holds exactly one effect, so folding several conjurations' sustains into one minor cannot be said -- and that clause is the whole value of the property, so the row is right to stay refused rather than ship the half that overcharges the wizard.

c.opportunity_instead().found: c.as_basic / Powers.instead -- near miss, already run down
c.opportunity_instead().why: Both f942 and f2607 ran this down: as_basic and Powers.instead file *refs* under a window, and a bull rush or an alchemical use is an action kind with no ref to file. Whatever closes it has to carry both, which nothing does.

c.oppose_attack().why: Nothing compares one attack roll against another - c.autohit, c.cancel and c.reroll_attack all act on the triggering roll without exposing a number to beat. i2019p1's second half (c.basic(harmless=)) is independently absent.

c.opt_in().found: c.pre_empt + c.instead_of / c.instead_of_now, used by the _riders helper in the same file
c.opt_in().why: f1099's clause is 'you can forgo X to instead Y', and pre_empt registers exactly that against a named row's clause, read back 'offered, never imposed' -- general_g's own _riders helper calls c.pre_empt(on_ref, what, swap). f1021 is the one that stays: its trade is on every implement attack rather than on a named row, so there is no (ref, what) to register against.

c.overrun(during_charge=).why: Both rows need a trait to rewrite how a charge *moves*, and actions.perform builds a charge out of a walk plus use(charge=True) before any trait sees it. c.overrun only works for the row making the move, which a trait is not; nothing in Cast reaches into the engine's own action handling.

c.oversized().why: The Weapon dataclass has ref/slug/damage/proficiency/reach/ranged/thrown/group/category/hands/properties/enhancement and no size field, and nothing refuses a weapon for being too big, so the permission has nothing to permit.

c.pact_boon().why: The boons are declared rows - features/warlock.py grants cf:warlock-f1c10 for the star leg and writes cf:warlock-f1s4's outright - so i2305p1's "nothing models the boon" is stale and c.pre_empt is what suppresses or replaces a named clause. i2343p2's "there is no bonus to add to" needs f1c10's hardcoded `c.bonus("attack", 1)` read through c.amount_for, which is one content line.

c.pass_on(attack=).found: nothing (c.pass_on handles conditions, c.redirect only an undeclared attack)
c.pass_on(attack=).why: p16049 wants a miss handed on to a creature already swapped with, after the attack resolved; `c.redirect` explicitly only re-aims one still being declared and `c.pass_on` moves a condition. Nothing re-aims a settled attack.

c.passes_through().why: overrun walks a creature through occupied squares and shuffles it into a free square at the end -- the printed 'must end its movement in an unoccupied square' -- which is both halves of what m884a4 asks for, including the refusal to stop there.

c.penalty(on_attacker=).why: resolve._mods(world, attacker, "attack", ctx) reads the *attacker's* own Mods, so a penalty imposed by the defender has nowhere to sit. The row also rules out the near miss (laying it on every enemy at arming misses anything that joins later) and f217 next door proves the holder-side version already works.

c.permit_charge().found: nothing to build - the permission already holds
c.permit_charge().why: m5303a0 looked in actions.charge and can_walk and found nothing refusing a charge to a burrowing creature, so there is no restriction to lift. This is a row whose printed trait is already true, not a facility anybody should implement.

c.phasing(when=).found: c.phasing / c.mode, Movement.ignores_when (the per-kind-of-going precedent), c.suspend_when
c.phasing(when=).why: f3116 says the verb exists and 'what it has no form of is a gate'. Movement.ignores_when shows the engine keying a waiver to one kind of going, which is half the gate the card prints. Not run down: modes are resolved by movement.mode_of rather than read through Mods with a ctx, so there is no lambda to hang 'while a named racial power is unspent' on.

c.pick_up().why: cf:swordmage-f0 says 'nothing anywhere picks one back up'. _picking_up is in the action menu as a minor action and its docstring names docs/blocked.json's cf:swordmage-f0 as the line that noticed. The row's second want, Gear.owned, is still real -- this symbol is not.

c.power_range().why: i2962x1 and i2771x1 say only 'a row's reach is header data and nothing lengthens another row's', which _stretched has answered since it began taking the row being measured as a gate -- the same evidence as c.reach_of(power=), and powers/sorcerer/level_6_t3 and level_2_t3 are the shipped examples.

c.quarry(nearest=False).found: nothing -- c.quarry measures from the ranger only
c.quarry(nearest=False).why: The nomination takes no second anchor, and cf:ranger-f0s1's other half is blocked behind the companion never taking a turn (#212), so even a kwarg would leave the feature half-dead.

c.race_components().why: f443 scales a payout by how many of a race's components the character carries. `c.race_of` and `Build.race` give the race, and nothing anywhere records per-race components as a countable thing a creature holds.

c.race_option().found: chargen.choices.race_options -- and it is the wrong thing
c.race_option().why: The top-ranked candidate ranks *races* for a class. f1521 needs which of five sub-options *within* a race is current, and says why c.element cannot stand in: two of the five are not damage types. The largest symbol in the queue and a genuine gap.

c.racial_power_used().found: a racial row's own header (cls="r1", "r2", ...), query.race_of and c.race_of, events.PowerUsed (carries the ref)
c.racial_power_used().why: Which refs belong to a race is header data already -- every racial power is declared with the race as its class -- so the watch can ask dsl.get(ev.ref).cls rather than hand-listing three refs and going stale on the fourth, which is the only reason this row says it cannot be written.

c.racial_row().why: `_named_traits` already swaps '<name> racial trait' for '<ref> racial trait' and `rt:` refs are real rows, so the mechanism exists; f2472 and i2301x1 report that their particular grant 'names it in prose' and the spec gives no ref. Check those two against the `rt:` index and `_named_traits`' coverage -- this looks like a miss in the swap rather than its absence.

c.raise_bonus().found: c.change_amount / c.amount_for -- and m1031a4 is in the registry
c.raise_bonus().why: Both stated holds are gone. Checked the registry: m1031a4 *is* declared, so there is a bonus standing to be raised; and change_amount exists for 'make a named mechanic hand out a different number', with amount_for as the read half. The remaining work is making m1031a4 read amount_for, which is the contract that family documents.

c.range_to().why: query.distance is geometry and reads no modifier at all, and nothing in the movement or targeting path consults a per-creature distance scale. Halving a measured distance has nowhere to be stored.

c.reach_bonus().why: f1995 says 'nothing rewrites it for a creature', which is flatly contradicted: _stretched exists because 'the target's reach increases by 1' and 'add your Wisdom modifier to the range of your ranged powers' were stored and never consulted, and a dozen content rows now lay those keys (ardent/level_2_t1 lays both). m6579a1's reach that follows a state is a gate lambda, since a modifier's gate is read at use time.

c.reach_of(power=).why: dsl.area_of calls _stretched with ctx {"power": p.ref, "kind": r.kind} and Mods.total applies the modifier's own gate to it, so one named row's range line is already rewritable -- powers/sorcerer/level_2_t3.arcane_power gates exactly that way and p12305's docstring says 'c.bonus("range", ...) exists and dsl._stretched reads it with the power in context'. f1817 (a literal inside another row's body) and f3432/f3434 (ranged turned melee) are different gaps.

c.reappear(after=).why: A thirty-day return has no clock: the engine's longest duration is the encounter and chargen says persistence does not exist. Narrative rather than mechanical.

c.recall_weapon().why: f612 says picking a weapon off the floor 'landed this session, but that is adjacency' -- and the only range in that path is `where.square not in here` inside `_picking_up`. The state change (append to `gear.weapons`, `gear.wield`, despawn the Item) already works; a recall at twenty squares is the same three lines without the adjacency test.

c.recast(no_provoke=).why: A creature-level 'your ranged and area attacks do not provoke' is written for an armour item, so a no-provoke may be lendable for the length of one use instead of living in Power.no_provoke. Not run down: whether the provoke test reads a creature modifier or only the header.

c.recast(reach=).why: dsl._stretched reads Mods.total(key, ctx) and area_of hands it ctx={"power": p.ref, "kind": ...}, so c.bonus("blast_size", n, when=lambda ctx: ctx.get("power")==ref) widens one named row today -- f287, f601 and f1010 are writable (f1010's own docstring already found c.widen_areas). Two caveats: _stretched clamps with max(0, ...) so f2202's narrowing is still unsayable, and f725/f2819 change the range *kind* (close burst to area burst), which no modifier does.

c.recast(usage=).why: c.recast changes what a row costs; nothing changes how often it may be used. c.restore_use hands a spent use back and c.forbid takes a row away, but no modifier moves a row between usage classes. f3292's other hold (Target.square) is separate and also open.

c.redirect_damage().why: f3702's own docstring names the gap: "c.pre_empt(ref, clause) is that window and 29 rows wait on it" - and both halves are on Cast now (cast.py:6769 and :6864), with each registration becoming its own action-menu entry. "Instead takes ongoing damage equal to what you would have dealt" is a registered substitution for the damage clause.

c.regain_points().why: p16440 says 'c.spend_points only takes them', but transfer_points already writes `theirs.points += gone` on a PowerPoints pool and PowerPoints.refresh sets points back to maximum. Handing points back needs a one-way door onto a write the engine already makes.

c.regeneration(suppressed_by=).why: unless= 'reads state at the moment of the tick' and is documented as the printed 'its regeneration does not function that turn' shape; _regenerates takes a doused label and skips the tick while a hold with that label stands, and level_11/controllers_sa.py:3612 calls it with one. m2068a3's 'there is no flag anywhere for this to flip' is the flag.

c.reload().why: m6507a0 and f396 both say loading is not a cost the engine charges at all, and `engine/ammunition.py` confirms it: a piece is drawn automatically when a ranged attack is declared and no action is ever spent. There is nothing to make cheaper.

c.remove_from_play().why: m6092a2 says there is 'no primitive for taking a creature off the board and bringing it back'. Condition.REMOVED exists with Rules(cannot_act, cannot_move) and _f3463_vanish is a working 'out of play until the start of your next turn'. Caveat: REMOVED does not lift the body off the grid, so an untargetable version may still be owed.

c.replace_roll().found: c.reroll_attack (writes AttackResult.natural/total), c.treat_roll_as (writes parity on the result), SavingThrow and SkillCheck are Decisions announced before being acted on
c.replace_roll().why: All three kinds of d20 are rewritable before they are honoured, so a stored face may go through the same path reroll_attack uses with a fresh die. Not run down: whether hit and critical recompute from a written `natural` outside the interrupt window, which is the whole reason treat_roll_as refused to fake the die.

c.reroll_attack(all_targets=).why: f715 was already re-pointed here (#496): `c.reroll_attack` rerolls the triggering roll off `c.trigger`, and an area power's other rolls are resolved before this fires and are not carried on the event. There is no second roll to find.

c.reroll_attack(ev=).found: c.reroll_attack (rewrites AttackResult.natural and total, honouring second-roll modifiers)
c.reroll_attack(ev=).why: The arithmetic works and only the event is unreachable, so handing a watcher's own event in is a thin door for p12321. Not run down: whether the watcher's event carries `result` -- and i2068p1/i3280p1 want a reroll banked for a later attack, which the verb cannot do at all and is a separate gap.

c.reroll_attack(rolls=).why: By PowerResolved every miss has already resolved, so a roll turned into a hit buys no damage and no rider -- the whole set has to be rerolled and what each new number lands replayed, which nothing does. p10354 and i1675p1 reached this independently and i1675p1 settled for the narrower rule.

c.reroll_attacks_against().why: c.reroll_attack reads off c.trigger, so it can only answer a roll this creature is being offered -- it cannot make an enemy reroll, and there is no standing roll-twice modifier for attack rolls. The damage side has exactly that (c.reroll_damage with c._rolls_twice_higher, and c.damage_disadvantage laid on another creature), which is good evidence the attack-side twin is genuinely absent rather than misnamed.

c.reroll_check(standing=).why: c.arm_trigger is precisely a reaction left lying in wait for a duration that charges the watcher the action a trigger costs - which is the "once per such check" half - so p16650's "none of them can be left lying in wait" is doubtful. What I would check is whether c.reroll_check can be handed the event rather than reading c.trigger; seven sibling verbs (c.unsave, c.autohit, c.halve, c.reduce, ...) already take an explicit ev=.

c.reroll_crit_die().found: c.reroll_damage and c.reroll_ones are the near misses, both wrong
c.reroll_crit_die().why: i2299x1 wants the second roll kept, and reroll_damage keeps the higher ('the opposite of what is printed') while reroll_ones replaces only dice under a floor. Both are read in _roll_damage as mod keys, so the shape is there, but no key means 'take the second result' and the critical rider itself is applied by engine/equipment.py from an item column.

c.reroll_damage(keep=).why: The keep= vocabulary exists on both roll-again siblings, and reroll_damage already works by laying a 'damage_twice_higher' key read in _roll_damage. Not run down: a 'keep the new result' variant needs a third branch there -- would check _roll_damage reads a second key cleanly.

c.reroll_damage_dice().why: All four rows argue only against c.reroll_damage (roll the expression twice, keep the higher) and none mentions c.reroll_ones, which is the other mechanic: each low die is replaced individually, the new face stands, and it is read inside _roll_damage where the dice are in hand. below= is the threshold and ref=/keyword= are the narrowings these cards print. What a count= would add is 'as many dice as you like' rather than 'the low ones'.

c.reroll_initiative(keep=).found: c.reroll_attack / c.reroll_save / c.reroll_check, all of which take keep=
c.reroll_initiative(keep=).why: Three of the four d20 rerolls take keep: str = "new" and implement {"new", "best", "worst"} with the same two-line dict; reroll_initiative is the only one without. i2966p1's own docstring already says keep="best" is 'what every other reroll on Cast already understands' -- the convention is there and the kwarg is not.

c.reroll_ones(sneak=).why: c.reroll_ones exists, is read inside _roll_damage "where the dice are in hand", and its ref= narrows to one row's dice - so f3749's "c.reroll_damage rolls the whole thing twice instead" is stale. The striker rider's roll carries detail='cf:rogue-scoundrel-f4' (quoted in c.hide's docstring), which is the ref the sneak= kwarg was asking for.

c.reroll_ones(when=).found: c.reroll_ones is c.bonus underneath, and c.bonus takes when=
c.reroll_ones(when=).why: The verb's body is `self.bonus(what, below, on=who, until=until, stacks=False)` and Mods.total applies each modifier's gate, so plumbing when= through is the whole change; f2705's two conditions (rage.in_rage, c.wielding) are closures that need no context at all. i3374x1's combat-advantage clause is the exception -- _reroll_floor calls Cast.total with no ctx, so a gate about the target has nothing to read.

c.reset_trap().why: `Trap.sprung` is a documented field whose own comment reads 'a pressure plate that has gone off and not reset', and `terrain.arm`'s `EnterSquare` watcher fires again the moment it is false. Resetting is one field write onto a component built to anticipate it.

c.reshape_area().why: widen_areas grows a burst and move_zone carries a shape elsewhere; turning one shape into another around a fixed square is a third operation, and i1836x1 adds that a row's reach is header data.

c.reshape_weapon().found: c.weapon_dice (writes the per-character `replace(w)` copies in Gear.weapons)
c.reshape_weapon().why: 'Weapon is a column set no body rewrites' is stale: weapon_dice rewrites one character's own copy, absolutely and with no reader needed, and group and dice are fields on the same object. Becoming a different weapon is that write with two more fields.

c.resist(once=).found: c.resist's own gated path, which already delegates to c.bonus(once=)
c.resist(once=).why: When when= is passed, c.resist returns self.bonus(what, amount, kind=f"{ref} resist", when=when) -- and c.bonus already takes once=, documented as 'the bonus ends after the first attack that could use it', spent by watching the roll. 'Against a single attack' is that kwarg forwarded one level; c.conceal and c.ignore_cover already forward it the same way.

c.resist_from().why: p16372 says 'the damage context carries power but no attacker'. That is stale: #302 added `source` (who is dealing it) plus `from_attack` to dmg_ctx for exactly this sentence, and resist_ctx is `{**dmg_ctx, ...}`. c.resist already takes when=, so the gate is writable now.

c.restore_use(item=).why: The engine appears to model no item consumption at all outside a weapon/consumable flag on Gear, so it is not clear there is an expended item to hand back. If a consumable's power is an ordinary row with a use, c.restore_use(ref) already is this whole row - that is the one thing I would check.

c.restrict_action().why: conditions.py already carries a condition whose entire effect is 'No standard actions. A shape you assume rather than a thing done to you -- it still moves, and it still acts otherwise', which is i3479p1's 'cannot take a standard action' and m5449a0's dormant clause without PETRIFIED's helplessness. Encounter.can_spend reads the Budget slots, and m193a3 already writes one from content, so narrower bars are reachable too.

c.retarget().why: `c.transfer` moves a live hold to another creature but 'refuses a hold carrying a relation or a subscription and returns None' -- which is exactly m976a2's sustained grab, a relation with an `on_sustain` subscription. Nothing re-aims a standing effect at a new target.

c.retrieve(consumable=).why: i2067x1's premise is wrong -- drawing *is* an action the engine spends (actions._wielding charges the printed minor) and c.draws_free(only=) already makes it free for a named ref. Not run down: Gear holds weapons, so a consumable has nothing to be drawn, which may be the real gap.

c.retrigger(ref).why: f2091 widens another row's printed Trigger. `on=Trigger(...)` is header data read by the dispatcher before any body runs, and `pre_empt`/`instead_of` substitutes *body clauses* only -- nothing edits a header for one character.

c.retype().found: c.deals / Cast._retyped (a held override that beats a printed type), f1646's DamageRolled mutation keyed on a ref
c.retype().why: An override for a duration exists and is read in the damage path, but it is keyed to the creature's WEAPON or IMPLEMENT rows rather than to one named row. Not run down: whether m3378a5's attack carries one of those keywords, in which case c.deals is the row today; if not, the f1646 watcher pattern is the fallback.

c.retype_damage(dtypes=).found: f1646's DamageRolled/Window.BEFORE mutation of ev.dtypes keyed on ev.detail, c.counts_as_keyword (+ Powers.granted_keywords, read in dsl.keywords_of)
c.retype_damage(dtypes=).why: Both halves f1231 calls missing sit in the tree: a feat beside it already adds a second type to another named row's damage, and a keyword can be granted per creature per row -- 'header data no trait can add to' is what counts_as_keyword exists to work around. It does not answer f1639/f1659, whose rider rolls no damage to catch.

c.roll_twice().why: A standing 'roll twice and take the better' held on the creature and consulted as the dice come up already exists on the damage side, which is the mechanism this row describes wanting. Not run down: p16678's own note implies the card is not about damage, and which roll it *is* about decides whether this is a one-line sibling or a real gap.

c.rolled_maximum().why: c.maximise's docstring says _max_of computes the ceiling and is private, and both it and c.reroll_ones are read inside _roll_damage "where the dice are in hand" - so the comparison i1577x1 wants is available at exactly the site two verbs already use. I would check whether DamageRolled can be flagged there.

c.run().why: There is no run action: actions.legal offers power, move, shift, charge, stand, escape, second_wind and the rest, and running is on none of its branches. Three of the five rows name actions.legal directly and agree.

c.running_start().found: powers.monk.second_card_1._running_jump -- a per-row calculation, not a flag
c.running_start().why: rt:r51-t1 needs a standing 'always considered to have a running start' and c.jump takes a number of squares and nothing else; _running_jump just hands it a bigger number itself. No mod key or Movement field is consulted by c.jump, so there is nothing for a trait to be true of.

c.save_disadvantage().why: The roll-twice-keep-lower pattern exists imposed on another creature for damage, laid as a modifier and read at the roll site. Not run down: durations.save is where a saving throw is rolled -- would check it can consult such a key.

c.save_order().why: Effects._on_turn_end rolls save-ends holds at TurnEnd and nothing moves the moment. i499x1 notes the keyword half is already answerable through keywords_of, so the whole remaining benefit is the timing.

c.save_vs_forced().why: i2494x1 is accurate: forced movement is shortened by `c.resist_forced` or refused by `c.immovable` and is never saved against, so there is no throw for a bonus to attach to.

c.second_initiative().why: `_double_turn` is already 'an elite or solo acting twice a round: a spliced second initiative slot', written as `c.extra_turn(init.rolled + 10)` and described as 'the shape m192a0 already settled'. m5553a0/m5719a0/m2069a2 all refuse on the grounds that `c.extra_turn` takes a count rather than rolling a second die -- a fidelity quibble about where the second slot sits, not a missing facility.

c.see_from(who).why: Borrowing another creature's square for line of sight and effect is written and held for a duration, so the attack-relevant half of this row exists. Not run down: measured_from is the only reader of the borrow and it covers ranged, area_burst and wall only, so whether melee reach and perception also need to honour it decides how much is left.

c.set_build().why: Build.choices is written once when the character is built; cast.py touches Build in three places and all three read. Nothing puts a character on another class's leg at runtime, which is precisely what the granted options' own `if not c.build(...)` gates need.

c.set_defence().found: query.defence(world, eid, d, ctx), c.bonus(when=, once=True)
c.set_defence().why: 'Your Fortitude equals 25 against that attack' is readable as a delta: `query.defence` returns the live value including level, mods and conditions, and `c.bonus(FORT, 25 - that, when=<this attack>, once=True)` scopes it -- the gated-modifier pattern `cf:ardent-f0` and m3842a3 both use. Nothing needs an absolute-set field.

c.set_origin(by=).why: cast_from is this card: 'determine line of sight and effect for your ranged and area attacks from the target rather than from yourself', held standing, read in dsl.measured_from so the borrowed square decides what may be aimed at as well as where the line is traced -- and its docstring names 'the stat block trait that says the same thing about a servant'. Laid on the sibling with who=this creature, it is the printed sentence.

c.share_space().why: f3670's "two creatures in one square is not a thing the grid allows" is stale: c.shares_space is the standing property that makes a square enterable and reads back through movement.shares_space, and share= is the per-move form. The gate the benefit hangs on can be true and can be asked.

c.shares_space(always=).found: movement.shares_space (a creature-level Mods key, already blanket), c.shift(share=True), c.overrun
c.shares_space(always=).why: m5808a0's claim that 'c.shares_space pairs the caster with one named creature' is wrong -- it lays a standing per-creature flag that lets anybody in. But it is the *occupant* side, and this card wants standing permission for the *mover*, which exists only per move (share=True) because movement._occupied asks the occupant and never the mover. What I would check: whether _occupied could read a mover-side key, and where the size test would live.

c.shift(swap=).found: c.swap, c.shift(share=True) -- neither is the rule
c.shift(swap=).why: m4617a0 needs the *destination rule* for every shift the creature makes changed; c.swap trades two squares on demand and share= lets a step pass through an occupied one. Nothing hangs a narrowing on a future shift.

c.shift(through=).why: `_through_them(c, squares_, kind="shift")` already covers a stated number of squares straight through whoever is in the way, calling `movement.overrun` with the printed kind, and exists because 'five cards here print a *shift* of a stated length through enemies' spaces'. f3320's objection is about `share=True`, which is the wrong lever rather than the missing one.

c.shift_as_teleport().found: Powers.pre_empts ('p10439's shift is replaced by two of them'), feats.battlemind_b._f3286_teleport and _f3290_teleport
c.shift_as_teleport().why: Substituting a teleport for a named row's shift is written and chosen as a variant before the shift happens, which is this card's 'instead' without needing an interrupt. Not run down: whether i2654x1 names a row or means any shift the creature makes, which pre_empts cannot key on.

c.shift_becomes_move().why: A shift a row grants is taken inside that row's body with the number in hand, and nothing intercepts one -- the same finding feats/exploits.py reached independently for f980's 'move 3 instead of 2' riders, which it marked c.movement_instead(squares=).

c.shift_while_prone().why: actions._movement returns empty for a prone creature before the shift branch, so the kinds of movement are off together. c.waive is the nearest verb and its word list is deliberately closed to four Rules fields - attack, halve_speed, grants_ca, speed_cap - with an unrecognised word raising rather than being accepted.

c.silence().why: i3470p1: 'sound is not modelled, so the zone would be an empty shape'. Nothing in zones, query or conditions represents noise or hearing -- the only sensory model is light and line of sight.

c.skill_circumstance().why: SkillCheck carries actor, skill, total, success and bonus, and skills.check takes skill, dc, who and bonus - no target and no purpose anywhere. f946 names both halves exactly and i693x1 confirms a check's context has no room for "against one sort of creature".

c.slowed(mode=).why: m6608a1 and m6610a1 agree and the engine agrees with them: slowed is a Conditions.Rules speed_cap on the creature, Movement.modes is a flat dict of mode to speed, and a speed modifier means every mode at once (general_h.f1337 says so). There is no per-mode cap and c.ignore_condition would make the creature immune instead.

c.speed_of(while_charging=).why: The attack context carries `charge`, so a damage- or attack-side gate on charging is already writable. Not run down: speed is read during movement rather than from an attack context, so whether a 'speed' modifier can see that key is the thing to check.

c.split().why: m1981a3 wants one creature to become two independent bodies sharing an initiative count. `c.summon`/`c.conjure` put new entities on the board but nothing divides an existing creature or shares its slot.

c.split_weapon().why: Gear holds a list of Weapon profiles and c.as_weapon appends one, but nothing divides an existing item into two or ties the halves together; no candidate came within range.

c.spring_trap().found: components.Trap (ref, plus a 'gone off and not reset' field), query.can_act's trap branch ('could never make the attack they exist to make'), c.use_power(who=)
c.spring_trap().why: The model expects a trap to attack as itself and use_power acts on another entity's behalf, so firing one may already be sayable. Not run down: nothing in content or the loader ever constructs a `Trap`, so check whether a trap can be on the board at all -- the story engine that would field one is unbuilt.

c.stabilise().why: Nothing holds a dying creature short of healing it, so the death-save the card interrupts never happens. i3094p1 has already written the half that is writable (c.end_effect on the untyped burns) and named this as the rest.

c.stance(keep=).why: c.stance ends whatever stance was live by definition and at most one is ever held, so two at once has no spelling. Nothing else on Cast holds a second stance slot.

c.stealth_speed().why: skills.modifier totals ability, half level, modifiers and the armour penalty and has no speed term at all, and SkillCheck carries no movement, so there is no penalty to waive or soften. m3222a5 states it precisely and three unrelated files reach the same conclusion.

c.store_damage().why: i1028p1 needs two absent things: a bank on the item for damage dealt, which Magic does not carry (the same gap as c.charges), and a specific self-inflicted damage source to pay out on. Neither exists, and ctx['source'] cannot stand in for the second.

c.store_points().why: i1980p1/p2 want an *item* that holds power points; `c.points`/`c.spend_points`/`c.transfer_points` all read the creature's own pool and there is no second place to put any.

c.store_roll().why: No component banks a d20 result, and m6191a4 needs one substituted later for an arbitrary roll by an arbitrary creature. Same family as c.bank_reroll() and neither has a candidate.

c.store_row(ref).why: i3324x1 wants one item to remember another item's row. `c.link` joins two *squares* for movement, and `Item` carries ref, owner, uses and a spend callable with nowhere to hold a second item's ref.

c.stored_dose().why: apply_poison coats a weapon with a rider the calling row supplies, and a dose has no identity a second row can reach for. Nothing reads back what effects a creature is under or what type a burn is either, which is the other clause's hold.

c.stored_row().found: c.borrow_row is the pick-at-use-time workaround, not a store
c.stored_row().why: cf:wizard-arcanist-f0s4 says Powers holds known, prepared and expended and 'a stored row is a fourth state the tome owns'; i540p1 and i3320p1 want a row or an item ref held *by an object* and c.grant_row hands one to a creature. Nothing in components.py records either.

c.strip_resistance().why: Both edit Defences.resist directly and hand the entries back on the hold's on_end -- one type save-ends, and all of them for a duration -- so 'c.resist grants one and nothing takes one away' is false twice over, and p16586 can hang the strip on the escalate hook it already has.

c.substitute_check().why: c.reroll_check rerolls the same skill; standing a *different* skill's result in for a failed one has no expression. The distinction is the row's own and is correct -- a reroll and a substitution are different rules.

c.substitute_condition().why: c.immune refuses a condition outright and c.worsen adds one; nothing intercepts an incoming condition and swaps it for another. c.pre_empt substitutes a clause but only where the row laying it reads instead_of, which an arbitrary incoming condition does not.

c.summon(count=).why: m2331a2 says c.summon 'names nowhere for the vacated footprint to go', but the second positional argument *is* a square -- so 'each square it formerly occupied now contains one m2332' is a hand-written loop over query.squares(world, me) calling c.summon per square, which the global rule allows (it mints no rows).

c.surface().found: c.terrain -- the fight, not the ground
c.surface().why: Grid carries light and difficult-terrain labels and nothing about what a square is made of, so there is no liquid surface for a movement mode to be granted over.

c.surges_of(ref).found: Health.surges / max_surges, c.surge_value(of=), c.spend_surge(on=), c.regain_surge(on=), c.no_surges(on=)
c.surges_of(ref).why: m1978a5 says 'nothing tracks another creature's surges or spends them from outside', and both halves are wrong: `surges`/`max_surges` are plain component fields and four verbs already take `of=`/`on=` for somebody else's pool. Reading the count is a door onto state that works.

c.suspend_effect().found: c.suspend_when, c.ignore_condition, durations.Effects.save (its context carries the effect, its label, conditions and ongoing types)
c.suspend_effect().why: Suspension exists for an effect you hold a handle on, and the save path knows exactly which effect is being rolled against. Not run down: whether SavingThrow.against identifies the effect well enough to find it again in world.effects.of(target) and hand it to suspend_when.

c.sustain(ref).why: Effects.sustain exists and actions._sustaining already drives it from the menu, including the two cases the default does not cover (sustaining early, choosing between two effects). What is missing is a Cast door and a way to find the effect, and c.dispel already finds holds by their label. p14124's 'has no verb' is literally true and 'has no mechanism' is not.

c.sustain_free().why: m4460a4 says 'a free one is not a cost the sustain machinery takes'; sustain_cost is typed `ActionType | None` and actions._sustaining only asks `encounter.can_spend(actor, eff.sustain_cost)`, which FREE satisfies. c.effect, c.aura and c.zone all already take sustain=.

c.sustain_grab().found: c.effect(sustain=) + c.on_sustain, c.grab(by=), c.conjure's returned eid
c.sustain_grab().why: c.effect takes a sustain cost and c.on_sustain is "what happens each time this effect is sustained", which is the announcement m6346a1 says nothing makes; and c.grab(by=) names a grabber other than the caster, which a conjuration's eid could be for i2393p1. I would check whether escape.attempt tolerates a non-creature grabber and whether a grab effect can be given a sustain cost.

c.sustain_row().why: f2842 says 'sustain= is a header field of the row that lays the hold', but the header only seeds a per-*effect* field: actions._sustaining offers the action for any effect whose sustain_cost is not None, and content rows pass it straight to effects.apply (warlock/level_5, bard/level_2). Setting it on the hold p377 laid is the clause.

c.telepathy().why: f3322 records that the racial trait carrying the range (`rt:r46-t2`) is declared `out_of_combat` and deliberately inert, so no creature carries a telepathy radius; f2470/f3317/f3395 each drop only the radius. No component field holds one.

c.teleport(no_sight=).why: c.teleport picks its destination through the decider and asks no sight question, so neither the permission nor the printed penalty for an occupied square can be written.

c.teleport_as().why: c.shift_as is the same sentence for a shift and is implemented as a standing change actions.legal reads back; c.grant_action's docstring names the extension recipe for a new word. The teleport itself works. Nothing new is needed but the word and its reader, which is what shift_as already cost.

c.teleport_bonus().why: c.squares_for's docstring writes the worked example as `c.teleport(c.squares_for(c.ref, 8))` and c.extend_move's is "one more square on every swordmage teleport" - so "nothing lengthens a blink" is stale and the rows need only read their distance. The one genuine residue is a blanket bonus to *every* teleport, where extend_move wants a ref.

c.terrain('outdoor').why: The reader exists; what is absent is data -- `terrain.dress` writes blocking squares, difficult squares and traps and never a terrain word, so `world.terrain` is always empty. By the `cf:fighter-weaponmaster-f3s0` precedent ('the gate is false today; it is asked anyway because it is the card's own sentence') f2718 is writable now.

c.tome_powers().why: Upgraded from my own `probable`, deferring to slice 6. I marked it probable because I had not run it down; the agent did, and found `_tome_power` is live and reaches the dailies through `c.borrow_row`, walking the level ladder the card describes. A hand verdict outranks an agent's by default -- but not when the agent is the one who did the reading.

c.trade_accuracy().found: c.may (a per-use election), Weapon.thrown (no heavy/light split -- powers.warlord._heavy_thrown says no weapon in the model carries it)
c.trade_accuracy().why: Two holds and both are real: the weapon property is absent from the table, and c.may asks once when a trait arms where this card elects per attack, so there is no per-attack choice to offer.

c.transfer(from_attack=).why: At the interrupt the effects the attack is about to lay do not exist yet, and c.transfer moves a live one -- a later question than the card asks. Nothing reads a pending effect list.

c.transform(into=).why: c.reanimate keeps the same entity's own numbers and c.form/c.mode change conditions and speeds, not the stat block. Nothing replaces a creature with a different one, which is m5787a0's whole printed effect.

c.transform_item().why: i2611p1 needs a magic item's base column swapped mid-fight, and the critical rider it names is applied by engine/equipment.py from that same column -- the Magic component records what the item may be laid on, not a live choice. Unlike a Weapon in Gear, nothing reads the base per use for a row to rewrite.

c.treat_as_enemy_for_cover().why: Confirmed absent by the author with two greps, and independently: c.cover_in lays cover in a zone by side, and nothing reclassifies who blocks whose line per pair.

c.trigger_trap().why: A trap's attack is a closure on `EnterSquare` keyed to its square, resolved through `resolve.attack` with the trap as attacker, so the attack path works and is reachable. Check whether a door can fire it without a creature actually entering -- the closure returns early unless `world.get(ev.actor, Health)` exists, so 'set it off from a distance' needs a victim or a refactor of `arm`.

c.triggering_attacker().why: The facility the symbol names exists, and its own docstring says the marker that stood on two rows 'wanted a method for a field the event has'. f619 still cannot be written, but for a different reason -- p3323 arms a watcher whose firing emits nothing -- so this marker needs re-aiming at that absence, not implementing.

c.uncrit().why: f976's docstring states it outright: 'result.critical is writable and a critical can be *demoted*'. _next_blow_of_mine_crits proves the site -- the Hit interrupt window, writing both the event field and the live AttackResult, because the outcome is recomputed from that object. f3523's 'there is no moment at which a roll can put it back' is contradicted by a working helper in the tree.

c.underwater_penalty().why: c.terrain("aquatic") says where the fight is and nothing anywhere charges a penalty for it, so i3050x1 has nothing to waive. The gap is the rule, not the waiver.

c.undouse().found: the `doused` label convention in monsters.level_09.brutes._regenerates, plus c.end_effect
c.undouse().why: m1155a4 says there is 'no way to ask is this creature's regeneration switched off and no way to switch it back on from another creature's trait'. Asking is `any(eff.label == DOUSED for eff in world.effects.of(other))` and switching it on is c.end_effect, which exists for taking a live effect off early; content already imports these helpers across level files. The caveat is that each row chooses its own label, so the two blocks must share a constant.

c.unsave(succeed=).why: c.unsave turns a success into a failure; nothing anywhere writes saved = True, so there is no other half. Writing the cost alone would be a row that only hurts.

c.unseen_by(sense=).why: cast.py:8811 and :8833 grant blindsight and tremorsense as Mods keys with working ranges, query.sees_in answers for both, and c.has_sense asks after one on somebody else - so i2413x1's "tremorsense is not a sense the board has" and i1470p1's "blindsight is not a sense the board keeps" are both false. A row skips the hide per enemy with c.has_sense(..., on=foe).

c.untargetable().why: `c.cannot_attack(on=foe, against=me)` cancels at `AttackDeclared` so 'nothing is rolled and no rider fires' -- which is 'cannot be attacked' read from the attacker's side, and m5746a3 already uses the verb. m5848a2's and m5746a3's claim that 'nothing bars a creature from being a target' is wrong; the thin part is applying it per enemy.

c.use_power(origin=).why: The engine's only entry point for one row using another already takes an origin square, and c.use_power simply does not pass one through. A pass-through kwarg, which is the thinnest door in this slice.

c.uses_this_turn(ref=).why: Powers.times counts uses for the whole encounter and last_round holds a single round number, so neither can say 'twice this turn'. The row also names the second half -- the once-per-turn limit has to exist before anything can add to it -- and the distinctness clause on top.

c.vestige().why: The same read as c.active_vestige(): switching which of a set is live is a labelled hold that c.endable swaps and c.lingers_label reads, and c.build already records the leg. What is genuinely unrecorded is the set itself, which is the chargen sub-choice shape - I would check whether anything can hold a two-item pick per character.

c.vulnerable(by=).why: The kwarg already exists and its comment names this exact card shape: 'eleven rows print a scope -- "vulnerable 10 to the <monster>'s attacks", "vulnerable 3 to weapon attacks"'. The damage ctx carries 'source' and 'power', so 'vulnerable 3 to **your** elemental attacks' is a gate on those two. cf:sorcerer-elementalist-f2s0's 'c.vulnerable takes an amount and a damage type with nothing on the attacker's side' predates #471.

c.wall_walk().why: i3016x1: 'the grid keeps a height and no surface to stand on sideways'. Grid has no vertical surfaces for a creature to occupy, and c.mode/c.phasing grant ways of crossing a square rather than a place to stand.

c.water().found: c.terrain -- the place, not the squares
c.water().why: All three rows need which squares are liquid, how many are contiguous and which are empty. Grid has no such feature and c.terrain answers only what sort of place the fight is in.

c.weapon_range().why: i1101x1 says 'Weapon.ranged is a column no body can reach'; c.weapon_dice reaches Weapon.damage from a body and its docstring explains why it needs no reader -- Gear.weapons holds per-character replace(w) copies. The same pattern on Weapon.ranged is a sibling verb, not a new mechanism.

c.widen_area().why: Both levers exist -- `widen_areas` lays a `blast_size` modifier for close blasts and bursts, `resize_aura` changes a live aura's radius and announces it -- but `cf:ardent-f0` is deliberately 'a snapshot, not an aura' and hardcodes `c.within(5)`, so neither reaches it. Check whether that row can be made to read its own `CloseBurst(5)` header plus `blast_size`; the facility is one layer from f3321.

c.worsen_save().found: c.reroll_save(keep="worst") (triggered rows only), Cast._rolls_twice_higher and the damage_twice_lower key as the shape
c.worsen_save().why: durations.Effects.save rolls once and consults no 'twice' key, though it builds a rich context for gates, so a standing roll-twice-keep-lower across every save against one attack's effects has nowhere to live. The damage path has the analogue and the save path has none.

c.zone(side=).found: Zone.owner exists and no terrain property reads it
c.zone(side=).why: Read the component: Zone carries owner, but Zones.difficult_squares returns a plain square-to-kind dict and blocks_sight is documented as 'binary and symmetric: it blinds both sides, which is terrain'. obscured is directional through the looker's senses, not by team. So nothing keys a terrain property on a side, and the field a side would hang off is unread.

cf:barbarian-f1s0.why: The ref is printed on cards and no row in the tree carries it - features/primal_shadow.py:19 says so directly and docs/blocked.json asks for it, and items/waist.py:384 is a third row waiting on the same absence. This is a content declaration gap, not an engine one.

cf:monk-f0c0.found: the five refs appear only as a list in content/items/implement_b.py
cf:monk-f0c0.why: No `@power` declares cf:monk-f0c0..c4 anywhere in content/features, so c.use_power and c.borrow_row have nothing to point at. The gap is content -- declare the five per-tradition rows -- and nothing stands in for them.

cf:monk-f0c1.found: nothing -- cf:monk-f0 is declared, cf:monk-f0c1 is not
cf:monk-f0c1.why: Checked the registry: cf:monk-f0 is in REGISTRY and cf:monk-f0c1 is not, so the five per-tradition attack rows really are undeclared. c.flurry_of_blows() has already landed and i724x1 records that it was not the hold; this is content that has not been written, not a facility.

cf:monk-f0c2.why: The five flurry cards are declared - FLURRIES = ("p7448", "p11207", "p13123", "p16131", "p16132") - and c.flurry_of_blows() derives from the registry which one the monk holds, "so a row can watch it, spend it, or hand back a use". f3701 does exactly that watch today; implement_b.py:114's "none of the five is declared" comment is stale.

cf:monk-f0c3.why: i1197p1 says cf:monk-f0 hands out one attack row per monastic tradition and 'none of the five is declared', so c.use_power(..., again=True) has nothing to point at. The symbol is an undeclared ref, not a missing facility -- it is content to write, and nothing in the tree stands in for it.

cf:monk-f0c4.found: nothing -- the five refs are named in a todo tuple and declared nowhere
cf:monk-f0c4.why: grep finds cf:monk-f0c0..c4 only inside items/implement_b.py's FLURRY tuple; no @power declares any of them. This is content work (write the per-tradition attack rows), not an engine gap -- c.use_power(again=True) is already the payout the rows want.

cf:sorcerer-soul-nat20.found: nothing -- but no engine work either
cf:sorcerer-soul-nat20.why: cf:sorcerer-f0s2 lists this rider among its own dropped clauses and i2693x1 says 'the natural-20 rider this card loosens to a 16 is that row's own dropped clause, so there is nothing standing for a wider trigger to fire'. The ref is simply undeclared; the natural roll is on the attack event, so this is a content row to write rather than a facility to build.

cf:warlock-f1c0.found: nothing -- cf:warlock-f1s0 names it and no row declares it
cf:warlock-f1c0.why: The ref appears only in prose and in i1015x1's todo; the pact boon row is undeclared. Content work, and i1015x1 is right that once the row exists its running value is the row's.

cf:warlock-f4c0.why: f2035 says the curse its pact boon reads 'has a ref and no row' -- so the gap is an unwritten content row, not an engine facility. Nothing else in the tree stands in for it, and f2035's other half (the boon hook) is separately open.

cf:wizard-arcanist-f0c1.why: The option has a ref and no row, and nothing makes one row count as a different sort of row -- both halves are absent, so even a declared option would leave this card unwritable.

cf:wizard-arcanist-f0c3.why: Checked: cf:wizard-arcanist-f0c3 is not declared. f2030 has already been re-aimed once (c.use_power would fire f2023b in a line), so the ref with no row is the whole of what is left. Content that has not been written.

cf:wizard-expert-mage.why: The class feature is in no content module, so there is no block for summon= to declare and nothing for c.summon_inline to place. p13984 is explicit that everything else on the card is the standard summoning the engine already applies.

chargen.armor_proficiency().why: No candidate. Armour proficiency is a build-time grant and chargen records none.

chargen.multiclass_powers().why: f1120 is explicit and has already dropped its other marker: c.rolls_with exists, and what is missing is provenance -- "'Gained through a multiclass feat' is a provenance Powers.known does not keep: a row is in the list or it is not, and the list does not say how it got there." Nothing in chargen records it either.

chargen.power_choice().why: power_options already scores and picks among candidate power refs when a character is built, and Sheet.choices plus c.build() is how a row reads a build decision back -- so 'no body can make this pick' is wrong. What I did not run down: Sheet.choices is a *derived* set over typed fields (leg name, primary, element, beast, race) with no slot for 'which of these N cards was taken', so recording the pick needs a new Build/Sheet field. f2694 also waits on cf:monk-f0c1..c5, which are not declared.

chargen.power_swap(pool=).why: `chargen.power_swap` already derives the pool from the feat's own `Power.swap` descriptor and removes the lowest qualifying row deterministically, so a swap with a filtered pool exists. f2697 wants the pool widened to another class's augmentable at-wills and the removed ref recorded -- a field on the existing descriptor plus a write, not a new facility.

chargen.proficiency(choice=).found: proficiency=('w3593','w3596') -- a fixed tuple, not a selection
chargen.proficiency(choice=).why: The header grant arrived and is not the hold: f2624 needs 'one of your choice', and nothing in chargen records a per-feat argument. Same gap as c.race_option() and feat.damage_choice().

chargen.race_choice().why: f604's "there is no race on a character to hold one" is stale - Build.race exists and RaceLine.granted() puts exactly one of a choice-list's rows into Powers.known, which c.knows reads back; f795 in this same slice says so outright about rt:r33-t0. The residue is the sub-choices that are not powers (f3214's skill, f2617's aspect), which want their own narrower symbol rather than this one.

chargen.retrain_on_rest().why: power_swap is a one-way trade made while the character is dealt. components.Afflictions states outright that an extended rest does not exist in this engine and chargen has no persistence, so there is no moment at which a hand is re-dealt.

chargen.second_fork().why: cf:warlord-marshal-f0 was re-aimed here precisely because `chargen.BUILDS` exists and 'adding legs does not supply it': the class's six legs are already spent on one printed fork, and a character takes one leg and stays on it. A second, independent fork per class is a different shape and nothing models one.

chargen.skill_training().why: Nothing in the vocabulary comes close, and that agrees with the rows: skill training is settled when a character is built and chargen has no door for it.

conditions.Rules.wake_on_damage.why: The rules table has no wake-on-damage term and resolve.deal_damage ends no unconscious hold, so there is nothing for this clause to suppress. Honestly marked rather than left looking finished.

dsl.Power.energy_types.why: f3435 has already ruled out the wrong readings: c.choose over damage types says 'either result' (psion_b.f3307 does it) and c.element answers a build's single sworn element. What is absent is the set to choose from -- no header field declares which types a variable-energy row offers.

dsl.powers_of(cls).why: `_arcane_rows` filters `dsl.REGISTRY` by `row.cls`, `row.usage`, `row.level`, `row.attack is not None` and a keyword to produce 'the attack rows an arcane character class prints, by ref' -- which is this symbol under another name. For f3209's theme-gated set, check whether theme rows carry a readable `cls`; the filter itself is written.

durations.keywords_of(creature).why: c.counts_as_keyword adds a keyword to this creature's copy of a *named* row, read through dsl.keywords_of and nowhere else, and c.rattling is the one creature-wide keyword grant - so the holder exists and only the wildcard does not. I would check whether granted_keywords can take an "any row" key, which is the whole of f1538.

etl.item.inline_block().why: _own_page cuts an item's text at its second `<h1>`, which on 12 pages is the inline stat block of the creature the item conjures, so none of its numbers reach the spec. dsl.Summon and c.summon_inline are complete and have nothing to be handed.

etl.monster.ability_text().why: m3333a0, m3333a1 and m3571a7 each report that extraction yielded the action and the usage and no other line -- no range, no defence, no damage, no effect. Nothing in the ETL recovers a block's text from elsewhere, and per CLAUDE.md #360 this shape is a bad import, so these are `defect=` territory rather than a verb to build.

etl.monster.summon_ref().found: c.summon_inline covers the engine side; nothing links the summon text to a monster ref
etl.monster.summon_ref().why: m5626a6, m3788a6 and m4008a2 all say 'no ref names the swarm this summons' -- the brief gives a printed name only. c.summon(ref, at=) and c.summon_inline(spec, at=) exist, so the gap is an ETL link column from an Effect line to a monster ref, exactly where the symbol points.

etl.monster.trigger_text().why: All four are extraction defects rather than engine gaps: one block is filed as an immediate reaction with no trigger line at all, and three print a trigger naming their own ref as something another creature possesses. Nothing in the tree can repair a trigger the compendium did not yield; this is the defect= shape.

events.DieRolled.why: f2151b needs an individual damage die announced, for 'you roll a 1 on a damage die'. The dice are visible only inside Cast._roll_damage, which reads reroll floors there precisely because 'DamageRolled carries a total with no dice behind it'. No event exists at that level.

events.HazardTriggered.found: c.hazard -- the zone, with no announcement
events.HazardTriggered.why: c.hazard builds a zone and bites inside its own handler, emitting only the damage. With no event p16445's trigger can never be declared.

events.InitiativeRolled.natural.why: f2807 already re-aimed off 'no moment exists' -- `InitiativeRolled` is emitted per creature by `turns._roll_initiative` -- and the residual is a missing field: the event carries `rolled`, the finished number with modifier and level folded in, where the card asks about the d20's parity. The second half is ordering: `start` rolls before `_arm_traits`, so no trait is listening yet.

events.Recharged.why: The function rolls the die and restores the row without emitting anything, so the moment the feat turns on is on nobody's bus. One emit would close it, but nothing stands in for it today.

events.Stood.why: actions.perform ends the prone hold and writes a Note; no event is emitted, so there is no moment for c.provoke to reach for. The same gap as ActionSpent.word seen from the other side -- ActionSpent does fire for the stand's cost but carries only the ActionType.

events.TrapTriggered.why: There is no trap event in events.py at all - grepping the module for "trap" returns nothing - and c.is_trap only answers what a creature is. The window m1526a3 answers never opens.

feat.associated_powers.found: build._associated_refs / _label_refs work -- the pages print no list
feat.associated_powers.why: The resolver is sound (general_g._associated measured 478 of 478 linked members resolving), so the gap is on the compendium side: f1113 and f3425 print no Associated Powers list at all, and f3425's docstring calls its own case permanent rather than pending. f1962 additionally needs which domain a character took, which nothing records.

feat.category.found: etl/feat._KINDS classifies prerequisites, which is a different question
feat.category.why: The feat table is (ref, id, tier, min_level, prereq, unparsed, books, spec) -- no grouping column -- so f1991's 'how many nearby allies have taken a feat of a particular category' has nothing to count. _KINDS labels the *kind of prerequisite* a feat gates on, not the family a feat belongs to.

feat.damage_choice().why: f2865 cites 'feat.weapon_choice(), which f2149 already carries'; f2149 actually carries c.chosen_weapon_group() and says 'a feat's arguments are not stored anywhere'. The gap is real and is one gap with chargen.proficiency(choice=) and c.race_option().

movement.step(per_square=True).why: f2417 is accurate and checked three ways: `movement.step` computes `left` against the destination, so a step between two squares both adjacent to an enemy provokes nothing from it, and `risk_along` and `_provokes_step` agree. The engine does not count squares, so there is no restriction for the feat to lift.

p4807.why: Keyword.RAGE exists and content/powers/barbarian/level_5.py and second_card.py already carry it on the class's dailies, so barbarian_rage's "a keyword nothing declares" is stale; and the row's own docstring already concedes that spending a use without running it is c.expend_row. The card itself is declared as cf:barbarian-f2c0, so the ref the marker names is a duplicate.

query.armour_ability().why: That helper already substitutes an ability in the AC formula by laying the difference as an untyped modifier -- `instead - max(dex_mod, int_mod)` -- which is exactly how a flat +2 replaces the term. The formula needs no reaching into; the armour type is readable off Gear.

query.armour_penalty(world, eid).why: skills.modifier line 93 returns `out + _armour_penalty(world, eid, skill)`, so armour and shield both cost a check and add - which makes i1872x1's and i2983p1's "nothing charges the penalty" stale. Only the read door and the *speed* half are open: chargen/__init__.py:96 reads speed_penalty off the table and nothing in engine/ applies it, which is i1181x1 alone.

query.bloodied(to=).why: Health.bloodied is read directly at every site that matters, so nothing can make another row's 'if bloodied' ask answer yes on account of a condition. No indirection exists to hook.

query.can_hide(world, eid).why: Content answers "may it hide" twice over from query.cover_between, so the components are there - but c.hide takes no precondition whatever (it grants the state outright), so there is no engine rule for p14032's permission to relax. I would check whether gating c.hide is wanted before building a query for it.

query.charging().why: OpportunityWindow carries kind_ ('walk, shift, charge -- movement.step's own kind') and its comment says it was added because 'why reads moved away for a walk, a charge and a flight alike, so "your movement during the charge does not provoke" had nothing to test. Four rows wanted them' -- which is m3547a1's second clause exactly. i1673x1 already reads AttackDeclared.charge. m5084a0's defender-side read is the one that still needs a door.

query.damaged_since().why: That helper keeps exactly this memory -- filled from DamageApplied, emptied at my own TurnEnd, 'stashed on the world, not in a module dict', memoised per (board, creature) and armed when the trait arms -- and four cards in that file already gate on it. i2803p1's 'nothing keeps that history' and i2303p1's 'nothing asks the world who has attacked whom since when' are both answered by importing it; the gap is a query-layer door.

query.fallen(world, side).found: resolve._die (the body stays an entity), Condition.DEAD, c.reanimate
query.fallen(world, side).why: m3535a3 says 'nothing enumerates the creatures that have already been destroyed'. _die keeps the body an entity and its initiative slot, lifts it off the grid and applies Condition.DEAD, and c.reanimate finds one by eid today. Only the author-facing pool is missing; the state is there.

query.in_sunlight(world, square).why: Both rows assert 'nothing on the board measures how bright a square is'; light_level does exactly that, worst-wins over terrain and dark zones, and its docstring says '13 rows wait on this; it is the model the other seven light symbols are written against'. Caveat: Light has no SUNLIGHT value, so BRIGHT does not tell daylight from a torch.

query.knocked_prone().why: Two helpers already roll 'a saving throw to avoid being knocked prone', keyed on `ConditionApplied` with `Condition.PRONE` and undone either by `c.cure` or by ending the hold that carries it. f3507's residual is narrower than the symbol: `ConditionApplied` does not say whether an *attack* caused it.

query.lit_by(world, ref).found: c.light (a radius held on the creature with kind=self.ref), query.light_level (reads the carriers out of Mods), Grid.light, Zone.obscured
query.lit_by(world, ref).why: The board is lit and unlit, and a row's light is recorded against its own ref and on a duration, so 'which square p1225 lights and for how long' is readable off the same modifier light_level consults. The row's note predates the light model.

query.phased_through(world, eid).why: movement.phasing answers whether a creature *may* phase, and Moved carries origin and destination and nothing about what was in between. The trigger the whole trait hangs on cannot be asked and there is no half to play without it.

query.run_penalty().why: A run is a move action whose only cost is the combat advantage it grants; nothing applies the printed attack penalty, so i1316x1 is right that writing the discount would be three points out of nowhere. The gap is the penalty, not the waiver.

query.shield_bonus().why: The number is in the armour table but chargen keeps only the shields' check_penalty and folds their AC into the build, and Gear.shield is a bare bool that loses light-versus-heavy. Nothing reports the contribution at runtime, which is what i2475x1 says. m4622a2 also needs a shield in a monster's hands, which Gear does not give monsters.

query.trained().why: skills.py's module docstring says it outright: 'There is no training model' -- a check is the ability modifier plus half level plus standing modifiers, and the +5 is not applied by default. i3225x1 adds that the blanket 'skill' key reaches every check, so 'untrained' cannot be narrowed. Agrees with the fixture's chargen.skill_training() verdict; Gear.trained is about weapons.

spec.feature_ref().found: etl.build._BARE_NAMED, build._believable, build._features, the cf: index
spec.feature_ref().why: The ETL already swaps a bare title-case class-feature name for its `cf:` ref -- `_BARE_NAMED` matches the run, `_believable` vets it, and the match is made against the `cf:` index alone. What f1219/f3626/f3645/i3523x1 report is that no `cf:` row exists for the features they name (i3523x1: 'a class the importer never brought in'), so check `etl.build.CLASSES` and `_features`' coverage against those features before calling the mechanism missing.

spec.monster_ref().found: etl.build._creature_names, etl.build._disease_names (both passed as `others=index` into monster.parse)
spec.monster_ref().why: A creature-name-to-ref swap already runs over every monster card, and ability names with it, so the ETL facility is not missing. Not run down: whether these particular creatures fail `worth_swapping` (one ordinary English word, all-mechanical words, under five characters) or simply have no row in the imported tier, which m1042a2's 'no ref in this tree' suggests.

spec.power_ref().why: The symbol names the wrong layer -- f3401's own docstring says the gap is suppressing the effect of a row being used, which is what pre_empt does ('you can X instead of Y', registered per candidate ref). Not run down: pre_empt needs the replaced row to read `instead_of`, and whether the five FLURRY rows do was not checked.

spec.ref.why: Swapping a printed name for a ref in a spec is a large existing ETL subsystem -- `_CITES` lists the verbs that take a power as object, `_BARE_NAMED` catches the bare possessive, `_cross_reference`/`_cross_reference_rest` run it over powers, items and feats. i1690x1 says it plainly: 'the spec prints that row's name where every other block in the file prints a ref', i.e. a coverage miss, not a missing facility.

spec.stat_block().why: query.stat_block is the engine reading the compendium row behind a creature. This symbol is the authoring brief rendering a stat block. A same-name near-miss across two layers, which is the shape the ranking will keep producing.

spec.subtype_block().why: m5092a0 reports one ref shared by three printed sub-templates with nothing in the loaded numbers to tell them apart. The ETL has no sub-template split for monsters (`_SUB_OPTION` handles power and trait sub-options only), so there is nothing to read.

spec.summon_block().why: The power spec carries the summon's behaviour and none of its numbers -- no defences, hit points, size or speed -- so there is no block to build a Summon from, and writing one would be inventing the numbers.

spec.weapon_ref().found: etl.sanitise.weapon_names; content.loader spawns monsters with `Gear()` and an empty weapons list (cast.py:10460 says so)
spec.weapon_ref().why: Two halves, and the deeper one is not the ETL: a monster carries no weapons at all, so even with a ref in the spec there would be nothing for a 'requires a flail' gate to read. The requirement is vacuous rather than mis-pointed.

turns.short_rest(surges=).found: the row's *other* claimed hold is closed by triggers.after_short_rest / ShortRested
turns.short_rest(surges=).why: The symbol itself is real: turns.short_rest restores encounter powers and does not spend healing surges, so a running song would have nothing to add hit points to. But the row also says 'nothing announces a rest', and that is false -- ShortRested is emitted and triggers.after_short_rest reads it, so the song can be started today and only the payout is blocked.
